ProjectDescription: This project evaluated the nutrient and fine sediment removal capacity of biochar amended soils for stormwater treatment in the Lake Tahoe Basin. Biochar is a natural material produced in forest fires or from burning biomass in controlled pyrolization kilns and can be amended in soils to increase moisture retention, infiltration and vegetative vigor. This research included (1) laboratory analyses on NDF biochar material; (2) experiments with flow cells to evaluate the best mixtures of biochar amended materials to optimize infiltration and pollutant removal; (3) experiments with a meso-scale physical model of a bioinfiltration swale to test BMP treatment efficiency.

The air quality constituents currently monitored are Ozone, Carbon Monoxide, Oxides of Nitrogen, Particulate Matter 2.5, and Particulate Matter 10.  More information can be found at laketahoeinfo.org and airnow.gov.

ProjectName: DL Bliss State Park Cultural Resources Inventory
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Comprehensive survey and documentation of archaeological and historical resources located in park unit. Efforts to identify historic properties in the park involves archival research, reviewing historical maps, and intensive coverage pedestrian survey. The survey will likely identify artifacts, features, and archaeological sites associated with ancestral Washoe occupation along and early Euroamerican land use. Results will be reported in a cultural resources inventory report which will then be used to develop an updated interpretative program for the park unit.

ProjectName: Emerald Bay Maritime Heritage Trail
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: The project developed an underwater interpretative trail to highlight the history of Emerald Bay and Lake Tahoe’s culture of recreation by way of shipwrecks. The bay is the final resting place of several recreational boats, launches, and barges used on the lake during the early 20th century. Underwater interpretative panels were placed at four dive sites in Emerald Bay. Waterproof interpretive cards created for divers are available at the park’s visitor centers, local dive shops, and online.

ProjectName: North Tahoe Fire Hazardous Fuels Reduction and Defensible Space Project
ProjectDescription: The scope of work for this project was drastically reduced for several reasons. However, 501 of the original 1013 urban lots were treated for fuels reduction to remove shrubs, smaller trees, downed logs, and woody materials. The cut biomass was chipped and removed from the site. The project serves to improve forest health for the larger trees that are retained. It also improves the defensible space for neighboring structures. The hand thinning work was completed in 2021, and the scope of work reduction was approved by the funder early in 2023 allowing for the project to be closed out.

ProjectName: Lower Wood Creek Water Quality Improvement Project - Phase II
ProjectDescription: Phase II of the Lower Wood Creek Water Quality Improvement Project completed most components not constructed in Phase I.  The Incline Village-area project reduced the amount of fine sediment discharging into Lake Tahoe and helped Washoe County comply with its next 5 year milestone of the Lake Tahoe TMDL. Tasks included installation of stormwater infrastructure, treatment BMPs, and shoulder stabilization. Benefits include improved stormwater quality release to Wood Creek & Lake Tahoe.  Phase I and Phase II combined earned Washoe County 44 Lake Clarity Credits.

ProjectName: Upper Truckee River Watershed Partnership
ProjectDescription: The Greater Upper Truckee River Watershed Partnership is a collaborative initiative that will link a variety of existing resource conservation and restoration programs in the South Shore. The greater Upper Truckee watershed primarily includes the Upper Truckee River and Trout Creek watersheds, as well as adjacent watersheds, comprising most of Lake Tahoe’s South Shore area. The initiative has created two synthesis documents that presents the range of existing projects and a renewed focus on landscape planning for climate resilience. The initiative will continue to evaluate resilience and identify further opportunities for community, forest, and watershed protection and adaptation.

ProjectName: Barton Neighborhood Urban Stormwater Treatment
ProjectDescription: The project includes a stormwater treatment basin on California Tahoe Conservancy lands at the intersection of 2nd Street and Helen Avenue and associated overflow conveyances, sediment traps, drain inlets, curb & gutter road shoulder protection, and rock bowls for outlet protection in areas of the neighborhood with inadequate drainage or treatment. The improvements will address significant localized flooding in the the neighborhood. This drainage catchment flows to the Upper Truckee River Johnson Meadow Restoration Project site  (EIP project 01.02.01.0070), which was recently acquired by the Tahoe Resource Conservation District.

ProjectName: Pioneer Trail Safety Improvement Project
ProjectDescription:
Install dynamic speed feedback signs on Pioneer Trail on approaches. 
At intersection, install edge-lines and center lines, intersection warning signs for minor streets, intersection lighting, upgrade pavement markings, and widen shoulder.

ProjectName: Lake-wide Aquatic Plant (native and invasive) Monitoring
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription:
Lake-wide monitoring of aquatic plants is needed to understand the existing conditions of locations and extent of plant populations. This information is used to strategize aquatic invasive plant control activities. Monitoring includes in situ dive transects and remote sensing techniques LiDAR and high resolution aerial imagery.

This project also includes the development of a monitoring plan that will allow program managers to conduct future monitoring efforts consistently.

Lakewide transect surveys are conducted approximately every 2-3 years.

ProjectName: Ski Run Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Pilot- Laminar Flow Aeration
ProjectDescription:
Laminar flow aeration (LFA) utilizes air diffusers, air compressors and air lines to add millions of very small air bubbles to the entire water column with the purpose of making it an oxygen rich environment. The oxygen rich environment has the potential to increase decomposition of the organic layer at the bottom of a waterbody, or in this case the marina.  The organic layer is used as food for plants and by reducing it there is potential to reduce plant populations as well. This pilot project will test the efficacy of LFA in Ski Run Marina. 

Results are encouraging and additional funds are being sought to research results and expand treatment further into the marina channel (lake-ward).

ProjectName: Bobtail Truck Sediment Reduction Project
Watershed: Mckinney Creek, General Creek, Meeks Creek, Sierra Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: This project purchased a new bobtail truck. This piece of equipment is used for summer O&M and winter sanding operations and supports the fleet through continuous use of newly upgraded and efficient technology.  This replaces an older International bobtail dump truck. The bobtail houses the recently purchased Epoke sand spreading system and cannot be mounted without having the proper equipment and chassis.  Summer operations include collection and disposal of material generated from street sweepers, cleaning of drainages, vegetation debris and general infrastructure maintenance.

ProjectName: 2019 North Tahoe Regional Park Multi-Use Trailhead Improvements
ProjectDescription: This project included the restoration of the upper parking lot in the North Tahoe Regional Park and construction of a multi-use regional trailhead that will receive the North Tahoe Trail being developed and constructed by Placer County. This project also developed and constructed paved ADA multi-use access paths to the Tahoe TreeTop Top Adventure Parks course, tennis courts, and the Tahoe Unleashed dog park.  Approximately 62 parking spaces were striped, including three handicap spaces; installation of site amenities included bike repair stations, bike lockers and racks, and a bike wash station; and installed permanent BMPs for parking lot drainage.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Aquatic Invasive Plant Enhanced Fragment Control Pilot
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association (TKPOA) implemented an integrated approach to preventing invasive aquatic plant fragments from spreading into Lake Tahoe. In addition to standard skimming and collecting efforts, TKPOA is experimenting with a boat back-up station, a bubble curtain and "seabins" to prevent this spread. The back-up station allows for boats to remove plants from the boat prior to entering Lake Tahoe proper, the bubble curtain provides a barrier that helps stop fragments from exiting the Keys water ways, along with the seabins that act as a floating collector, collecting fragments stopped by the bubble curtain. This pilot project is in the west channel.

ProjectName: SNPLMA 15 Incline Village Prescribed Fire Project
LeadImplementerName: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
ProjectDescription:
This North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District project reduces hazardous fuels on at least 150 acres, but not more than 544 acres of local government owned land in the wildland-urban interface of Incline Village, Nevada to mitigate wildfire risk to the community and improve forest health.

The project promotes community protection and forest health by utilizing prescribed understory fire to cost-effectively reduce hazardous fuels and to protect life, property, and the environment from the effects of catastrophic wildfire. Understory burns restore resilient landscapes by reintroducing natural disturbance to a fire-adapted ecosystem.

ProjectName: Control of Hypoxia (Dead Zone) in Lake Tahoe
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Lake mixing replenishes oxygen in the deep waters of the lake. Climate change has altered the mixing regime of the Lake and it hasn’t mixed to the bottom since 2011, the longest period on record. The lack of mixing threatens to delete oxygen concentration in the deep waters of the Lake and could lead to the creation of dead zones that would yield fish kills and species shifts, along with an unprecedented release of algae-stimulating nutrients. This project will test methods to prevent or mitigate the threat. Methods could include improving the nutrient sequestering capacity of BMPs, exploring EIP project design, and will also contribute to our understanding of lake process and drivers.

ProjectName: Nearshore Human Health Monitoring
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription: Periodic monitoring of harmful microorganisms and toxins that affect human health is necessary to ensure public safety and recreational enjoyment of Lake Tahoe’s nearshore waters, and to inform possible management actions. The assessment included Fecal Indicating Bacteria (FIB), (which include total coliform, Escherichia coli (E. coli), and fecal coliform), and cyanotoxins, which can be produced during Harmful Algal Blooms (HAB) of organisms such as cyanobacteria.

ProjectDescription: The South Tahoe Greenway - Upper Truckee Bridge at Johnson Meadow Project will build upon the overall South Tahoe Greenway shared use path network through the south shore of Lake Tahoe. Elevations of the project area range from 6,230 feet to 7,800 feet.  The project would primarily consist of forest thinning and vegetation treatments in areas that have been previously treated within the past 15-25 years to reduce fuels for forest fires and promote healthy and resilient forest stands. ProjectDescription: California Department of Fish and Wildlife will analyze the abundance and distribution of non-native fish (mostly rainbow trout) along major tributaries on Lake Tahoe's west shore. The road has been replaced with a lower grade singletrack trail to enhance user experience and meet current standards.

The project will include a survey of the deepwater plants communities, a pilot project to exclude invasive species near deepwater plants, restore the native communities. The work will also contribute to a better understanding of the functional role of the native communities to lake clarity and the impacts of invasive species.

A subset of stocked LCT (25,000) were tagged with t-bar anchor tags to learn more about growth, survival, and movement in the Lake.  Stocking also served to provide the public an opportunity to learn more about this iconic species and provided a more diverse recreational angling opportunity in Lake Tahoe. Outreach and education on this project in 2023 included:  Washoe Tribe of California and Nevada Earth Day and SWEP environmental outreach day.

Starting in 2026, rapid response plant control work will be documented in Project # 01.03.01.0037 Lake-wide Surveillance and Assessments.

Funding will be utilized to complete needed field assessments and data analysis to determine the existing conditions that will be used to develop a proposed action and associated environmental review with public input. The LTBMU entered a Participating Agreement with TRCD in 2023 to complete environmental review.

Phase one of this effort is to completed needed environmental review ($100,000). Phase two (permits and implementation) would include habitat improvement actions such as spawning gravel enhancement, placement of large woody debris, riparian vegetation plantings, and/or fish management devices.

Forest fuel reduction project work will include forest thinning with hand crews, chipping (and removal of wood chips), stacking burn piles, pile burning and/or understory burning.   Project will treat a minimum of 200 acres, up to a maximum of 354 acres in: Burton Creek SP (up to 88 acres), Sugar Pine Point SP (up to 196 acres), and Emerald Bay SP (up to 70 acres).  The State Parks crew will be funded by both LTRA funds, and matching funds provided by State Parks.

ProjectName: Incline Park Facility Renovations

Project improves native forest composition and structure, reduce hazardous fire fuels, promotes increased carbon sequestration through increased future tree growth, and reduces potential greenhouse gas emissions from wildfire.  Treatment methods include mechanical forest thinning with tractors, removal of logs and chipped woody materials for utilization, and restoration/rehabilitation of recreation trail utilized by logging tractors for the project.

ProjectName: Kahle Complete Street Project

This 0.5 collector road provides key linkages to the existing Stateline to Stateline bike trail, trails throughout Rabe Meadow, and a Douglas County community center. EA 4H890

This study presents results from detailed chemical analysis of exhaust from snowmobiles as well as snow and surface water collected in Blackwood Canyon, a tributary to the west shore of Lake Tahoe and a popular winter recreation area for snowmobile riders.

ProjectName: Mysis Shrimp Removal
LeadImplementerName: UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center
ProjectDescription: Some of Tahoe's measured clarity decline is due to the introduction of shrimp and the subsequent loss of daphnia. Daphnia are exceptionally good at eating small (1-4 micron) algae and inorganic particles which are primarily responsible for Tahoe's clarity decline. Tahoe's warming surface waters, because of climate change, favors small algae because they sink slower. Reducing shrimp abundance to 27/m2 will allow daphnia to exist in the lake and result in improved clarity.

ProjectDescription:
The inventory shows that overall, progress is being made toward GHG emission reduction goals. From 2005 to 2018, the Tahoe Region’s emissions have declined significantly by 38.7 percent. Total emissions were reduced from 1,297,446 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent to 795,793 metric tons. 

For the first time, the updated inventory modeled carbon sequestration potential in Tahoe’s forests and meadows and compared those to annual emissions. The updated inventory found that the natural landscape sequestered or stored between 300,000 and 1,000,000 mtCO2e in 2018. This is compared to about 800,000 mtCO2e in emissions for 2018.

ProjectName: Lakeside Beach & Marina Aquatic Invasive Plant Control UV Light Pilot II
ProjectDescription:
This project expanded on the first UV Light pilot project by utilizing lessons learned and increasing the size of the treatment areas. The initial pilot showed promising results in that most treated plants exhibited signs of deterioration 7-10 days following treatment. This second pilot expanded treatment areas within the marina and off-shore locations at 1 acre each. 

This pilot is now complete, and new projects for Lakeside Beach and Lakeside Marina have begun as separate projects, tackling the entire infestation at both locations, using UV and bottom barriers.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Pilot- Laminar Flow Aeration Pilot
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association (TKPOA) implemented a pilot project using Laminar Flow Aeration (LFA) in a six acre area, west of the main lagoon of the homeowner channel. TKPOA investigated LFA's potential to reduce plant growth and/or densities by the increased levels of oxygen LFA creates.  The project was implemented in the spring of 2019 and is now part of the Tahoe Keys Aquatic Weeds Control Methods Test (CMT)- comparing effectiveness of multiple methods to address invasive aquatic weeds in the Keys. Performance of LFA will now be tracked as part of the CMT project.

ProjectName: Highway 89 Corridor Tahoe Trail Feasibility Study

The purpose of the State Route 89 - West Shore Tahoe Trail Feasibility Study is to identify a recommended alignment to complete the Tahoe Trail between Meeks Bay and Spring Creek Road. This is the final section of the West Shore Tahoe Trail and will connect popular recreation sites, including Emerald Bay and D.L. Bliss with a shared-use trail. 

The Feasibility Study was completed in 2022.

LeadImplementerName: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
ProjectDescription: The goal of the project is to complete the restoration of approximately 22 acres of Burke Creek and surrounding Rabe Meadow. Activities include partially filling Jennings Pond and constructing islands to prevent flooding and restore wetland habitat, filling man-made ditch on USFS land, improving trail conditions and filling man-made ditches to increase hydrologic connectivity in the meadow, and restoring Burke Creek channel at the Lake outlet.

ProjectName: IVGID Bocce Courts Project
ProjectDescription: The IVGID community-identified new bocce courts as a priority community service project. The courts were constructed in a community park for all members of the public to enjoy. The project included the construction of four (4) bocce courts, enough to host small tournaments or support a local league. The court complex allows the community to enjoy bocce locally, instead of driving out of town to seek these opportunities, adding a new recreation opportunity.

For funding and implementation management, Placer County has split apart the "Tahoe City Complete Streets & Highway Improvements" (EIP # 03.02.01.0024) into two separate, distinct projects.  The reason for the split is due to local funding and accounting of grant money.   Additionally, the two components of the originally-proposed project have separate timelines.

Located in the wildland urban interface and the State Responsibility Area Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone, this work builds on existing and planned treatments creating a contiguous area of reduced fuel loading, protecting multiple at-risk communities.  Work will strive to enhance ecosystem resilience against catastrophic wildfire, pest invasions, and climate change by, reducing forest fuels and stem densities and increasing heterogeneity and habitat diversity.

Construction began in the summer of 2022 and completed during the summer of 2023.

LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Department of Wildlife
ProjectDescription: In consideration of potential Lahontan Cutthroat Trout (LCT) recovery actions within the Lake Tahoe Basin, there is a need to understand if hatchery raised LCT are capable of persisting in the lake and spawning in its tributaries.  This project will gather information on spawning salmonids.  The goal of this project is to gain a better understanding of LCT dynamics in Lake Tahoe by utilizing hatchery fish and monitoring life and individual health/history indices (i.e., fork length, weight, K-factor, temporal and spacial spawning patterns, life span, etc.) from fish attempting to spawn in tributaries around the lake.  The construction of a long term management structure is planned for 2026.

ProjectName: US Forest Service Airport Eastside Fuels Reduction Project
ProjectDescription:
The recently completed Airport East project was a 37-acre hazardous fuels reduction project located within the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) of South Lake Tahoe, on lands owned by the City of South Lake Tahoe. 

Originally a 52-acre fuels reduction project, costs increases resulted in reduced treatment area. There therefore remains need to secure future funding to complete work on the remaining 15-acres of untreated land.

LeadImplementerName: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

ProjectDescription: This project will report on public lands acquired in the Tahoe Basin by the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit- United States Forest Service from 2008 onward.

ProjectName: AIS Educational and Rest Area Gazebo
ProjectDescription: Installation of a gazebo at the Meyers Watercraft Inspection Station to act as a shaded rest area and educational center for boaters that are waiting for their boat to be inspected and decontaminated.

ProjectName: Private and Local Government WUI Fuel Reduction-Tahoe Douglas, Nevada
Watershed: Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Glenbrook Creek, North Logan House Creek, Logan House Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Mcfaul Creek, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Trout Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Reduce hazardous fire fuels and implement prescribed fire on private and local government lands within wildland-urban interface (WUI) areas of Tahoe-Douglas Fire Protection District. Project represents current unfunded need of the Tahoe-Douglas FPD’s ongoing forestry and fire program to reduce hazardous fuels and restore forest health.

ProjectName: Lake Tahoe Curlyleaf Pondweed Control Strategy
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription: Dr. Sudeep Chandra of University of Nevada, Reno studied life history attributes of invasive curly leaf pondweed in Lake Tahoe to assist managers in controlling populations around the lake. Through lab studies and field observations, the efficacy of contemporary technologies used to control plants were evaluated.

ProjectName: Lake Forest Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
ProjectDescription: NTPUD owns the Lake Forest No. 3 water system which is located at the wildland urban interface in North Tahoe at the bottom of Dollar Hill. The water system is comprised of watermains ranging from 2 inches to 8 inches in diameter. The system is deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and does not meet current fire codes. The project would install 3,000 linear feet of new 8- and 10- inch watermains to replace the existing 2- and 3-inch diameter steel watermains. Three new fire hydrants would be installed that would be accessible from North Lake Boulevard.  The new upsized watermains would also be equipped with a connection point for an intertie with Fulton Water

ProjectName: Lake Tahoe Seasonal and Long-term Summer and Winter Clarity Trend Assessment
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription:
Trends in clarity, as measured by Secchi depth, vary between summer and winter seasons. The long- term summer trend is consistently declining, with a noticeable cyclic pattern. Winter clarity is showing a different long-term trend. The ongoing summer clarity decline effectively offsets improvements in winter, confounding average annual clarity restoration efforts. The cause for the diverging seasonal clarity trends has not been well documented.

This project conducts analyses of the watershed and in-lake monitoring data to evaluate drivers of seasonal clarity conditions.

ProjectName: Round Hill Fire Protection Water Infrastructure Tank
ProjectDescription: Construction of a water tank to increase water storage capacity by 150,000 gallons. This will increase fire protection and the ability to protect land during catastrophic wildfire .

ProjectName: Vactor Truck Replacement
Watershed: Bijou Park, Bijou Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: New Vactor Truck was received in August 2020 and has been placed into service. The Vactor is a critical piece of equipment for removing sediment, trash and debris from stormwater collection, conveyance and treatment systems. The purchase of this truck replaced an aged non compliant truck with a CARB emission complaint model to ensure the City is able to adequately maintain stormwater management systems.

ProjectName: Ski Run "Mountain to Marina" Green Infrastructure Planning
ProjectDescription: A green infrastructure approach to stormwater management protects, restores, and mimics the natural water cycle. The project involves planning, analysis, outreach, and technical assistance within the greater Ski Run/ Bijou Park Creek watershed to reduce stormwater pollution from developed parcels and roadways collectively. The project identifies opportunities and constraints for regional treatment, public/private partnerships and green infrastructure solutions that achieve multiple benefits. Work with the community and stakeholders produced support for recommended strategies.

ProjectName: Brautovich Park SEZ Restoration and Park Rehabilitation Project
ProjectDescription: The Brautovich Park SEZ Restoration and Park Rehabilitation was a joint effort between Douglas County and the Nevada Tahoe Conservation District (NTCD).  The Project restored over a half acre of a Douglas County-owned parcel (APN 1319-18-401-003) to historic stream environment zone (SEZ), relocated the existing baseball field and playground to less sensitive lands within the parcel, and upgraded the parking and water quality features to help achieve the Lake Tahoe TMDL.  The reconfiguration of the site incorporated improved stormwater treatment and erosion control to bring the parcel into BMP compliance.

ProjectName: Lower Kingsbury Area-wide BMP Retrofit
ProjectDescription: The project implemented an area-wide BMP retrofit project that installed linear rock-pool basins, an infiltration basin, double sediment cans with filter inserts and building dripline protection to prevent stormwater runoff from directly entering a tributary to Edgewood creek on constrained public and private parcels off lower Kingsbury Grade in Douglas County, NV. NTCD will work with TRPA to gather documentation to award parcel BMP certificates to associated parcels. NTCD will work with Douglas County to attain Lake Clarity Credits for the project.

ProjectName: Slaughterhouse Meadow Restoration Phase 2
ProjectDescription: This project restores 0.7 acres of poor functioning fragmented wetland habitat to functional cold-water aquatic and terrestrial wetland habitat and  addresses mosquito habitat, water quality, wetland function and diversity though the construction of a beaver analog pond structure. This project results in no net loss of wetland acreage.  Total project impacts to a WOUS is 0.70 acres. Total project boundary including upland is two acres. Project  results in approx 30 CY of relocated fill, 10 CY of rock fill for erosion protection along roadway and +/- 1,800 for export of pond material. Plan calls for salvage and reuse of all wetland soils and plants.

ProjectName: 56 Acres Master Plan
ProjectDescription:
The Project is the development of a master plan document for the City/County Park known as “56 Acres”.   

The purpose of the master plan is to develop a comprehensive strategy for the project site, facilities, programs and services that is responsive to the community’s demographics, social background, and recreational and health needs. The plan will serve to guide the City in a wide-ranging future capital implementation plan.

Projects resulting from this plan will be separate EIP projects:
1.	Rec Center
2.	Construction of Through Road (Tallac Avenue to Rufus Allen Blvd)
3.	Demolition of existing Rec Center
4.	Design and Construction of a new Campground

ProjectName: North Tahoe Recreational Access Water Quality Improvements (Phase 1)
Watershed: Griff Creek, Tahoe Vista, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Carnelian Bay Creek, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Lake Forest Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Blackwood Creek, Eagle Rock, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, General Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription:
Placer County DPW-Tahoe Engineering Division completed Phase 1 of the North Tahoe Recreation Access Plan (NTRAP) in 2021. The NTRAP provides a valuable resource tool for planning, maintaining, and developing existing and future year-round public recreational access areas for a range of user groups in the North Lake Tahoe Truckee regions. 

Phase 2 is implementation of improvements at trailheads identified in the NTRAP. The Lower Sawtooth Trailhead was the first site selected & improvements were completed in May 2025. The next trailhead proposed is located on Ward Creek at the Stanford Rock trail crossing. The County is currently seeking funding for the design & construction of the project.

ProjectName: Soroptimist Softball Field Renovation
LeadImplementerName: Soroptimist International of South Lake Tahoe
ProjectDescription: The softball field will be improved with the construction of new fencing, infield soil, outfield new sod and leveling, creation of a warm up area, new scoreboard, new back stop, PA system, bleachers, dugouts, water refill station/fountain, and a pathway from the Middle School parking lot to the new entrance to the ball field.  A portion of the parking lot will be removed in order to allow for the fencing and access to the warm-up area and BMPs will be installed.

ProjectName: TTD Transit Operations - Phase 2045
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription:
This project is a major expansion of core services and the addition of regional destinations. For the core local routes, operating days will be expanded; frequency will be doubled, including service to Meyers. South shore will be linked to the north shore via Spooner Summit; Incline Village to south Reno; express route from Stateline to Sierra-at-Tahoe; and microtransit at Daggett Summit. Four regional year-round (Fri-Mon) routes will be added-Truckee AMTRAK to Stateline Transit Center, Truckee AMTRAK to Homewood Mountain Resort; Sacramento connection to Stateline TC; and Stockton connection to Stateline TC.

ProjectDescription: Reporting on recent wildfire/natural disaster events have recommended end warning systems and hardening of communication systems for overall situational awareness that can influence emergency response and evacuations along the transportation system. These same communication systems are critical for day to day traffic operations and communicating with the traveling public. Public notification systems include broad technology improvements and a robust communications network with the ability to adjust to failures in the overall communication system and improve the delivery of end warnings to the public through artificial intelligence. The project will improve efficiencies of the roadway system.

ProjectName: Emerald Bay McDonald's Bike Trail
ProjectDescription: Complete reconstruction of a deteriorated bike trail located along the Emerald Bay Road McDonald's.

ProjectName: Al Tahoe Government Center BMPs
ProjectDescription: The Al Tahoe Government Center serves multiple jurisdictions and is a priority location for improved water quality infrastructure to stabilize sediment sources, treat runoff and alleviate flooding. Overflow from any proposed onsite facilities must tie into existing City storm drain system and discharge points on adjacent properties. The project will include assessing maintenance needs of these existing BMPs. TRPA will coordinate with El Dorado County and the City (and LTCC and USFS as needed) to plan and permit stormwater facilities needed for the parcel.

ProjectName: Permanent Watercraft Inspection Station- Meyers
ProjectDescription:
The Lake Tahoe Watercraft Inspection Program has proven extremely effective and serves as a national model. A permanent location for the Meyers Watercraft Inspection Station has been proposed on California Tahoe Conservancy Asset Lands that will allow the program to have enhanced facilities to maintain protection of Lake Tahoe and provide excellent services to the public.

To stay up to date on the progress of this proposed project, please sign up for updates here: 

https://public.govdelivery.com/accounts/CAELDOR/subscriber/new?topic_id=CAELDOR_777

ProjectName: Sonora Avenue Stormwater Project
ProjectDescription: The project will reduce scour of the unprotected road shoulders along Sonora Avenue by routing urban runoff to a system of underground storm drain inlets, sediment traps, perforated pipes for infiltration and underground conveyance pipes to the existing treatment wetlands (Osgood/Wildwood basins).  All drainage improvements will occur within the existing road right-of-way.  This project will provide underground drainage improvements to facilitate above-ground improvements associated with the Ski Run "Mountain to Marina" Green Infrastructure Planning initiative lead by the TRPA (EIP 01.01.01.0192).

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Tactical Green Infrastructure
ProjectDescription: The project involves watershed planning, stakeholder outreach and implementation of innovative stormwater technologies that reduce TMDL pollutants in the Tahoe Keys community of South Lake Tahoe, California. Project planning uses a regional stormwater treatment approach to identify opportunities for public/private partnerships and installation of innovative LID stormwater treatment.  Implementation of the multi-benefit project will improve water quality, enhance wildlife habitat, increase climate change resiliency, reduce wildfire threat, improve bicycle and pedestrian connectivity, and help protect investments in Tahoe Keys aquatic invasive species control.

ProjectName: SR 28 Marlette Creek Water Quality and Erosion Control
ProjectDescription: This project proposes to provide erosion control and stormwater treatment at directly connected outfalls from SR 28. Stormwater from State Route 28 will be captured and treated prior to entering Marlette Creek by constructing water quality treatment at each stormwater outfall.  Additionally, the project will stabilize SR 28 shoulders, road embankments, and dirt parking areas that are directly connected to Marlette Creek and alleviate ponding on SR 28.

ProjectName: Lake Tahoe Water Trail Lake Access and Stewardship Outreach & Education Campaign
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription: The Water Trail Multicultural Outreach Campaign and educational materials are designed to educate California’s diverse populations about water safety, stewardship, and responsible public access to human-powered paddling recreational opportunities using the public Water Trail launch/landing sites to help protect the watershed and shoreline plants and wildlife. Combining recreation with environmental protection, the Water Trail is a 72-mile water route along the shoreline that connects public launch/landing sites supported by educational wayfinding interpretive signage installed at 20 trailhead sites that include restrooms, trashcans, parking, paddle outfitters, and facilities.

ProjectName: Glenbrook Underground
ProjectDescription:
Undergrounding of all power lines in our small community will enhance fire safety, improve reliability of service, improve the scenic quality of the neighborhoods, and reduce insurance costs.  
Homeowners will contribute to a 501.c3 with the sole environmental purpose of putting these lines underground in our small community.  

As of the end of 2024, the project has reached 63% completion. Key progress includes connecting the Glenbrook utility spine to the substation and extending distribution/transmission lines to critical areas such as Back Road, Old Highway 50, Glenbrook Road, and beyond.

ProjectName: NV Energy Resilience Corridors Projecct
LeadImplementerName: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
Jurisdiction: Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Carson City County, NV

ProjectDescription: The project will create resilient forests adjacent to approximately 28 miles of NV Energy utility infrastructure on the Nevada side of the Tahoe Basin.  The project is designed to treat in 3 zones, Zone 1 is the area immediately adjacent to utility infrastructure (15'), Zone 2 is up to 175' from utility infrastructure and Zone 3 can extend up to 1000' feet from the utility infrastructure.  The project will thin forest to improve forest health, remove trees that could grow into or fall on power lines and reduce hazardous fuels.

ProjectName: Sugar Pine SNPLMA Round 16 Hazardous Fuel Reduction Phase 2
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: The SNPLMA Round 16 Phase 2 project will thin forest stands and reduce fire fuels on 150 acres within a 267-acre area of Sugar Pine Point State Park, continuing where Phase 1 left off.  The project is designed to reduce tree densities and surface fuel loading to modify potential fire behavior and reduce the threat of high intensity wildfire.  The project will also restore native forest composition, structure and function.  Forest thinning and fuel reduction treatments will include: hand crew thinning, chipping, pile burning and understory burning.

ProjectName: Evaluating the impacts of Road Salts on watershed and nearshore environments
ProjectDescription: Winter road management in the Tahoe Basin relies on application of de-icing compounds such as road salts to improve road safety. Unfortunately, such compounds are known from many field-based studies to have adverse environmental impacts.  The main concerns of increased salinity include reduction of infiltration along slopes draining to channels, increased erosion and fine particle transport, ecological and water quality impacts. While research on road salts have evaluated tree mortality and soils along highway corridors, knowledge of the impacts to streams, groundwater and nearshore environments is lacking. Watersheds identified are Incline, Third, and Glenbrook.

ProjectName: Lower Rosewood Creek Aquatic Organism Passage Project
ProjectDescription: This project proposes to remove two standpipe/metal culvert crossings installed in 2003 at Incline Way and upstream near an existing multi-use path and replace them with structures that allow for the passage of native salmonids, along with improving the floodplain connectivity in one location between the two culvert crossings.

ProjectName: Tunnel Creek Alternative Trail
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
ProjectDescription: The Tunnel Creek Alternative Trail is a Nevada Division of State Parks project, with partners such as Nevada Division of State Lands, Tahoe Fund, Great Basin Institute, and TAMBA. This 2.28-mile single-track trail starts at Tunnel Creek canyon's base, linking indirectly to the Tahoe East Shore Trail and the Incline Flume Trail. It addresses public safety issues on the congested, sandy, and steep Tunnel Creek road, responsible for many bike accidents every year. The trail will be built in two phases, expected to be completed by fall 2025.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Offshore Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Project
ProjectDescription: The 2019 Lake Tahoe Region AIS Action Agenda identifies this site as a Tier 1 priority for treatment. Aquatic invasive plant control at this site commenced in September 2020. Diver-assisted suction removal has been the primary method of plant control thus far. In September 2023, an aquatic invasive species, New Zealand mudsnail (Potamopyrgus antipodarum), was detected by contracted divers within the project area. Work was paused to reduce risk of spread of this species.When work recommences, future reporting for this project area will be documented in Project # 01.03.01.0051-South Shore Offshore Aquatic Invasive Plant Planning and Control, occupying all or portions of sub-units 7, 8, and 9.

ProjectDescription: In 2019 the Council completed an “Aquatic” Science to Action (S2A) plan describing recommended research and monitoring activities to better understand Lake Tahoe’s clarity condition and associated drivers. Acknowledging the need for prioritizing watershed science needs, the Council initiated an “Upland Ecosystem” S2A planning effort in 2020. The Council and its management partners subsequently developed a wholistic, basin wide S2A plan that updates aquatic priorities and links watershed research and monitoring work to the lake. The “Integrated” S2A plan provides the framework for linking resource management and science community priorities.

ProjectName: Upland Ecosystem Science to Action Plan (watershed)
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County

ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Science Advisory Council’s “Science-to-Action Plan for the Upland Ecosystem” provides a broad framework for collecting data, performing analyses, and developing the modeling tools needed to address restoration and resilience planning in the Tahoe Basin. A holistic and coordinated approach is needed to address climate change and disturbance impacts (e.g. wildfire, introduction of species) in forests and watersheds of the Basin. This framework addresses the research needed to identify changing conditions, inform resource management decision-making, and monitor expected outcomes. Project focus areas include forests and fires, terrestrial and aquatic linkages, and biological integrity.

ProjectName: Spooner Front Country Hazardous Fuel Reduction
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
ProjectDescription: This 42 acre project focused on creating defensible space around the new Visitors Center and other existing structures located in Spooner Lake and Backcountry State Park. All roads are managed as fire lanes to help ensure public safety and allow firefighters safe ingress/egress in case of emergency. Thinning prescriptions varied to meet a range of management objectives (i.e. defensible space, firefighter access, forest restoration) and included mechanical thinning, hand thinning, chipping, and pile burning. Wood mulch created through this project was used on-site for revegetation around the new parking lots.

ProjectName: Nevada Department of Transportation/Douglas County Shared Stormwater Decant Facility
ProjectDescription: The Nevada Department of Transportation (NDOT) and Douglas County have a need for a safe and effective way to decant and treat their stormwater from various maintenance operations in the Lake Tahoe Basin. The proposed facility will allow primary and secondary treatment of stormwater treatment byproducts such as water from drop inlets or sweeper material with wastewater eventually discharging to the sewer system. The facility also provides a safe and environmentally-friendly place to store materials and wash equipment.

ProjectName: 72-mile Lake Tahoe SCUBA Clean-up
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription: A volunteer based underwater clean-up focuses on remediating the subsurface of the lake bed via SCUBA. This project spans the entire 72-mile near shoreline circumference of Lake Tahoe. This stewardship project not only removes litter from the lakebed, but also educates the public and informs local stakeholders about the extent and types of litter accumulation in Lake Tahoe.

Jurisdiction: Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Carson City County, NV
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Tunnel Creek, Bonpland, Sand Harbor, Marlette Creek, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Glenbrook Creek, North Logan House Creek, Logan House Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Mcfaul Creek, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Trout Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: This pilot project was implemented to allow Clean Up The Lake to further investigate the submerged litter present below the surface of Lake Tahoe via SCUBA divers and a team of other volunteers. The skills, knowledge and procedures acquired through this pilot project will contribute to the success of the upcoming 72-mile Lake Tahoe SCUBA enabled clean-up.

ProjectName: Fallen Leaf Lake SCUBA Clean-up
ProjectDescription: In 2023 the CUTL dive team covered 4.84 underwater miles at Fallen Leaf Lake as part of a pilot litter collection project. During this remediation, the team found Fallen Leaf Lake to be the dirtiest lake in organizational history, based on litter items collected by mile. Over 10 days, the team collected 8,322.9 lbs of litter including 3,310 litter items. Notably the team removed 644 tires from Fallen Leaf Lake. The team was not able to complete a full circumnavigation of Fallen Leaf Lake due to a lack of funding. Clean Up the Lake is actively looking for funding in order to return to the lake to complete the pilot litter remediation and complete the establishment of a baseline litter dataset
