ProjectName: NTFPD Wildland Urban Interface Hazardous Fuels Reduction (NTFPD WUI HFR)
ProjectDescription: North Tahoe Fire Protection District will reduce hazardous fuels on at least 300 acres, but not more than 700 acres of highest priority WUI Defense Zone areas within North Tahoe and Meeks Bay Fire Protection Districts as identified in the Lake Tahoe Basin Community Wildfire Protection Plan. These treatments will improve forest health and reduce the threat of catastrophic wildfire, protecting life, property, and critical infrastructure in the Lake Tahoe Basin.

ProjectName: US 50 at Warrior Way Safety and Drainage Improvements
ProjectDescription: The project modified the intersection of US 50 at Warrior Way by adding traffic signalization and pedestrian crossing infrastructure. The project also proposes to construct a storm drain to capture and convey roadway runoff to a proposed water quality basin.

ProjectName: Sand Harbor Hazardous Fuels Reduction/Defensible Space
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
ProjectDescription: The primary objectives of this project were to reduce hazardous fuels and create defensible space within 150 feet of park infrastructure at Sand Harbor. Mature brush was hand thinned or masticated to reduce continuous fuel beds.  Large willow clumps were cut in select locations adjacent to park infrastructure.  Hand thinning of the forest focused on reducing tree densities and removing bark beetle infested and dead trees. Material not burned or hauled off-site was chipped and used on-site in high use recreation areas. Dwarf mistletoe in Jeffrey pine was reduced in a portion of the project.

ProjectName: Castle Rock Peregrine Falcon Habitat Protection
LeadImplementerName: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
ProjectDescription: Educational signage has been installed on route to a popular hiking and climbing destination and peregrine falcon nesting site. The goal is to reduce stress on the nesting peregrine falcons at Castle Rock by educating hikers and climbers of seasonal closures and nesting disturbance. Project includes installation of permanent educational signage at the North Benjamin Trailhead and temporary signage during the nesting season.

ProjectName: Upper Diamond Peak Hazardous Fuels Reduction and Healthy Forest Restoration Project
LeadImplementerName: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
ProjectDescription: Decades of fire suppression and increased development in forested areas have led to overstocked stands that present extreme fire risks to the Incline Village community and surrounding land. This project has reduced hazardous fuels and restored forest health on 72.6 acres of Incline Village's Diamond Peak Ski Resort property and privately owned land. The project complements previous, ongoing and planned fuels treatments as part of a larger cross-boundary forest management strategy, which will contribute $4.6 million in match/leverage. Reducing fuels in this FAP Priority Area will lower the probability of catastrophic wildfire, protecting local communities.

ProjectName: Forestry Education & Job Placement Program
ProjectDescription: Lake Tahoe Community College's Forestry Education & Job Placement Program will increase the skilled workforce urgently needed to accelerate the pace of forest treatments in Tahoe and will subsequently reduce wildfire risk. The program offers stackable certificates leading to an associate degree in forestry with transfer opportunities to 4-year programs. By offering multiple education and career pathways for youth and adults, the program aims to recruit traditional and non-traditional students and place students in jobs during and after program completion.

ProjectName: Vacuum/Rodder Truck Air and Water Quality Improvement Project
Watershed: Mckinney Creek, General Creek, Meeks Creek, Sierra Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: El Dorado County intends to purchase a Vac-Con Titan Truck. The total purchase price of the new truck is $500,000, of which the County will match 50%. The current vacuum truck is outdated and according to the California Air Resources Board (CARB) needs to be replaced ASAP. The new style trucks have a single engine design that greatly reduces CO2 emissions when compared to the old double engine, less efficient models. This will result in a large reduction of CO2 that meets current air quality standards and compliance with CARB requirements. The vacuum truck is also the primary equipment used to clean/maintain water quality BMPs and County infrastructure needed to comply with the Tahoe TMDL.

ProjectName: Making the smart connection: new sensor real-time technologies and ecosystem models to understand nearshore greening in Lake Tahoe
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription: Lake Tahoe’s nearshore water quality including algal growth is intimately tied to the internal dynamics within the lake (e.g. mixing and grazing by animals) and the supply of nutrients from the streams and groundwater entering the lake from the watershed. Our goals are to understand the linkage between the watershed and streams to the nearshore algal growth in Lake Tahoe. We will evaluate these linkages and monitor the water quality of the nearshore habitat by placing water quality sensors measuring temperature and oxygen at the outfalls of streams flowing into Lake Tahoe.

ProjectName: Lake Mill Meadows Project
ProjectDescription: This project addresses two ongoing habitat concerns at Lake Mill Meadow. This project 1) Adjusts the hydraulic gradient to facilitate terrestrial obligate wetland vegetation, and 2) mitigates an erosion feature in the lower meadow that was altering the meadow hydrology and causing a drop in the groundwater table resulting in loss of wetland/meadow habitat. Project Completed October 2021

ProjectName: Sierra Blvd-Palmira Avenue to South Tahoe Bikeway Connector
ProjectDescription: Project will construct approximately .134 miles of Class 1 Mixed Use Recreational Trail extending from Palmira Avenue on Sierra Blvd to U.S. Highway 50 (LTB) and from Lake Tahoe Blvd to the South Tahoe Bikeway located near Silver Dollar Avenue.  The proposed Class 1 bike trail connector will link the South Tahoe Bikeway with the Sierra Blvd Class 1 bike trail.

ProjectName: Bijou Park Class 1 Bicycle Trail - Greenway Connector
ProjectDescription: This project proposes to construct 0.6 miles of bicycle and pedestrian trail that would link the Al Tahoe Mobility Project constructed in 2020 (Johnson Blvd & Al Tahoe Boulevard) with the CTC Greenway Trail Phase 1B (Constructed 2021).  The trail would be entirely located within the City's Bijou Park Property.  This project is a high priority project with the Community Mobility Group and the Measure S Joint Powers Authority Bicycle Committee.

ProjectName: Johnson Boulevard Bicycle and Pedestrian Improvements
ProjectDescription: Project proposes to modify the existing Johnson Boulevard travel way from the southern limits of Al Tahoe Boulevard to the northern limits of Fairway Avenue per preliminary concept design contained within the LTUSD Safe Routes to School Master Plan by reducing roadway width, construction of a Class 1 bicycle trail, construction of sidewalk and ADA improvements, construction of minor drainage improvements as required for project, installation of pedestrian safety lighting, and pave and stripe roadway for Class II bicycle lane on west side.  The total project length is estimated to be 4,900 linear feet (.92 miles).

ProjectName: Cave Rock Water Quality Improvement Project
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Lands
ProjectDescription: Over the past few years, the Cave Rock unit of Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park has experienced a high level of unauthorized walk-in visitor use and user-created trails have led to severe slope erosion and sediment runoff above the beach area at the southern end of the Park. This project will prevent walk-in visitor access through temporary and long-term fencing, and repair existing erosion through a mix of slope stabilization and revegetation. The project will also assess the existing Tahoe yellow cress (TYC) enclosure in the Park for possible relocation or expansion to protect the sensitive habitat from human use.

ProjectName: Delineation of Asian Clam Populations at Sand Harbor State Park
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Lands
ProjectDescription: This project implements underwater surveys for Asian clams in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park at Sand Harbor to determine recolonization rate following treatment and delineate current extent of the invasive Asian clam populations. Surveying and continued monitoring took place over three years, with number of dead and live clams recorded at each dive’s conclusion. Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) flights will also be conducted to obtain aerial data on metaphyton coverage, and remote sensing of the clam survey area with UAV imagery will be used to assess potential growth of metaphyton associated with clam populations.

ProjectName: Rubicon Trail and Emerald Bay Site Improvement Project
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Reconstruct approximately 800’ of the Rubicon Trail; install two new interpretative panels, two new benches, install symbolic fencing, and directional signage; remove redundant trails and trail features; thin trees and vegetation to improve access to the shore of Emerald Bay, enhance views of Fannette Island, protect vegetation and water resources, clarify paths of travel for easier visitor use, and improve day-use trail network near the Vikingsholm Castle located at Emerald Bay State Park.

ProjectName: Hicks Erosion Control Project Phase I
ProjectDescription: The Hicks Urban Parcel is owned by the State of Nevada and is adjacent to Incline Creek. In the past few years, the site has experienced large scale surface erosion. The first phase of this project will analyze sources of erosion by completing hydrological, geotechnical, and topographical surveys, and prepare conceptual and 75% design documents for restoration and stabilization of the Hicks Urban Parcel. Construction of erosion control and hillside stabilization measures will take place in subsequent phase.

ProjectName: SR 28 Corridor Collision Reduction Improvements - Mackinaw Road to Grove Street (SHOPP)
ProjectDescription:
In Tahoe City on Route 28 from Mackinaw Road to Grove Street. Place green colored bike lane treatment or High Friction Surface Treatment (HFST), install recessed striping, rectangular flashing beacons, and signs, and construct curb ramps.  EA 0J922. 

PLA-28 Rehab Combine project (0J01U) combines PLA-28 Rehab (0J010) and Tahoe City Rehab Loc 2 (0J922).

ProjectName: Máyala Wáta Restoration Project (Phase 2)
LeadImplementerName: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California
ProjectDescription: The Máyala Wáta Restoration project seeks to restore approximately 283 acres of meadow habitat in Meeks Meadow though a number of techniques including conifer removal, vegetative treatments, and cultural prescribed fire. The overall goals for the project is to increase the density and frequency of culturally significant plants for traditional uses, and to get the Washoe people back on their homelands in the Tahoe Basin.

ProjectName: Meeks Meadow Biomass Removal Grant
LeadImplementerName: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California
ProjectDescription: The Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California and USFS/LTBMU are jointly implementing the Máyala Wáta Restoration Treatment. A component of this treatment is to mechanically thin encroaching conifers, and contractors will remove the high value logs from the site. However, the small diameter woody biomass targeted for removal is of low economic value. This agreement will help fund transportation and utilization of forest biomass generated from the Máyala Wáta treatment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions that may otherwise be emitted from open burning the material onsite. The Tribe will arrange for the transportation of an estimated 7,000 tons of forest biomass to facilities around the basin.

ProjectName: Lake Tahoe Future of Tourism Shared Vision and Destination Stewardship Roadmap
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: The Lake Tahoe-Truckee Sustainable Recreation and Tourism (aka Destination Stewardship) partnership developed a shared vision related to the future of tourism to the region as well as an implementation roadmap. The vision and roadmap serves as guideposts for collective decision making and tangible action steps for sustainable destination and visitor management.

ProjectName: Elgin Street Sweeper
ProjectDescription: Purchase of one (1) Elgin Street Sweeper to replace one (1) failing unit.  Project is requesting $75,000 in AQ Mitigation Funds and $75,000 in WQ Mitigation Funds.   AQ & WQ Mitigation funds will be matched with $146,000 in City of South Lake Tahoe General Funds.   Total cost of unit is approximately $296,000.

ProjectName: USGS Caldor Fire Impact Study
ProjectDescription: Extreme climate event such as persistent drought and catastrophic wildfires have the potential to change watershed processes and lake response. Wildfires can kill or stress vegetation, combust soil organic matter and change infiltration-runoff characteristics which leads to changes water quality in streams. The Caldor Fire burned more than 10,000 acres within the Upper Truckee and Trout Creek watersheds. The impact was particularly observed in upland basins of Saxon and Trout Creek watersheds, where 60 and 35 percent of the watersheds were burned, respectively. Cold creek, while having less than 1 percent burned, had 7 miles of bulldozer cuts and fire lines were used to control fire spread.

ProjectName: Watershed Hydrosimulations Grant
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Hydrologic simulations and analyses of simulations were completed to characterize the geographic distributions and temporal evolution of projected responses in averages, seasonality, and year- to-year variations of weather, snow, and streamflow conditions in response to an ensemble of climate-change projections. In addition to these simulations, grantee engaged with selected stakeholders to determine other specific targets for analysis and adjusted analyses accordingly, where the models used supported such targeted additions.

ProjectName: Airport Eastside Hazardous Fuels Reduction Project-Phase II
ProjectDescription: Hazardous fuels reduction in the wildland urban interface (WUI).  Specific to this project is improving controllability of fuel along U.S. Highway 50 (Community evacuation route) and to provide defensible space to critical airport infrastructure (apron areas used during wildland fire events and airport structures adjacent to areas in yellow.)  100’ is defensible space   Concludes protecting the eastside of the airport property boundary full length.  Total project treatment area is 20.65 acres.  This project includes a CEQA Tahoe Program Timberland Environmental Impact analysis for hazardous fuels reduction work funded by Round 18 by SNPLMA

ProjectName: Prescribed Fire Treatment at Airport for 2020-2021 CCC Treatment of Trees less than 14" dbh
ProjectDescription:
California Conservation Corps (CCC) were hired by the Airport to perform forest health hazardous fuels reduction on trees located outside of the Stream Environment Zone.  Treatment occurred in 2020 and 2021 concluding in November 2021 (South Lake Tahoe Airport Improvement Project).  
All trees were hand cut and stacked into burn piles for future prescribed burn after wood has cured.  El Dorado AQMD permits must be secured prior to any ignition. Per TRPA MOU MM a Qualified Exemption is required for this project. 
CCC will be hired to perform prescribed burns on behalf of the airport.

ProjectName: Fuel treatment effectiveness surveys, Caldor Fire
ProjectDescription:
The project surveyed fuel treatment areas impacted by the Caldor fire to measure fire effects to vegetation using standard measures of fire severity and tree mortality. This work compliments studies being carried out by other teams of fuel treatment influences on fire-fighting effectiveness and structure protection. 
A link to the report and more information in the project details below. 
The study found: Across all treatment types, trees were 3x more likely to survive fire in treated areas. Fire severity measures were significantly lower in treated versus untreated areas. The most effective fuel treatment was multiple entry mechanical and hand thinning followed by mastication.

ProjectName: Emerald Bay Gateway Project
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Modify and modernize the Vikingsholm Parking lot, which was constructed in the 1960's, to accommodate shuttle transport, tie in with planned bike path, rectify seep holes in parking area, install BMPs, remove concrete islands and redesign for snow removal, install a contact station and welcome center for visitors and staff with educational and interpretive elements; install ADA Accessible restrooms, install a covered veranda, provide for emergency response access and response resources, install solar power electrical systems, install security gates, upgrade and modify the entrance for visitor enjoyment, ADA access, and public safety for this iconic park.

ProjectName: Enhanced tributary monitoring to assess Caldor Fire impacts
ProjectDescription:
Enhance the Lake Tahoe Interagency Monitoring Program to:

(1) Increase the number of samples collected per year by 5 at impacted watersheds of at Upper Truckee at South Lake Tahoe and Trout Creek at South Lake Tahoe sites (an increase from 21 to 25 samples per year) and one control at Third Creek at Incline Village with the option for up to all LTIMP locations.

(2) Analyze water-quality samples for post-fire impacts on ammonium and dissolved organic carbon. Constituents will be added at 2 impacted and 1 control site (26 samples a year).

ProjectName: Emerald Bay Vikingsholm Pier Rebuild
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Rebuild the Vikingsholm Pier in Emerald Bay. The Vikingsholm Pier visitor dropoff walkway is in need of repair: the entire pier is in a state of deterioration with compromised visitor safety and is not accessible to boats during low water years nor is it compatible with water taxi service. The pier and path to the historic core of the Vikingsholm estate are not ADA accessible from the lake.

ProjectName: Emerald Bay Vikingsholm Restroom Replacement
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription:
Replace and improve the Emerald Bay restroom facility. 
Emerald Bay welcomes up to 1,000 boats per day and more than 10,000 visitors per day during busy summer weekends. Vikingsholm has one very old restroom which was constructed in the 1960s - due to its age, the restroom is deteriorating and is not ADA compliant.  This is a beautiful and iconic park and the restroom facility that serves these thousands of visitors is no longer up to the task.

ProjectName: Wildfire Smoke Impacts to Lake Tahoe’s Water Quality
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV

ProjectName: Emerald Bay Boat Camp Pier ADA Access to Campground
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Improve trail access from the proposed ADA Accessible Pier to the Boat Campground for ADA access and compliance.  Campsites will also be improved for compliance and access.

ProjectName: Tahoe State Recreation Area Campground Pier Rebuild and ADA Access
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Construct a new pier at Tahoe State Recreation Area Campground in Tahoe City. With the completion of the bike path adjacent to the campground, substantial increased use of campground trails and pier is causing degradation of infrastructure.  Some boards on the pier have been replaced for public safety but the pier and its pilings need to be rebuilt in entirety. Additionally, CDPR would like to improve ADA access from the paved bike path to campground trails and pier.

ProjectName: Sugar Pine Point Bike Trail Repair, Beach Access, and Erosion Control
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: The paved bike path was installed through the Z'berg preserve without a guiding maintenance plan. The paved bike path has deteriorated and is no longer safe for bikes. Visitors ride bikes from the paved bike path down the sandy trail and stair access to the General Creek Mouth Beach, resulting in substantial erosion of very sensitive soils - this erosion runs directly into Lake Tahoe. Required components of this project include erosion control, signage, interpretation, bike rack installation, repaving the existing bike path, and installing appropriate BMPs.

ProjectName: Sugar Pine Point Visitor Center and Historic Water Tower Project
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Cooperative project with Sierra State Parks Foundation- The existing visitor center is not ADA Accessible, was not designed as a visitor center, and needs major modification to this historic building, and major redesign of educational and interpretive elements. Connected historic water tank element is falling apart and requires major work for stabilization to maintain this important element of the story of the Ehrman Mansion and early Lake Tahoe settlement.

ProjectName: Sugar Pine Point Day Use Foot Bridge Replacement
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Upgrade footbridge in Sugar Pine Point Day Use area. Current undersized footbridge is causing ongoing erosion issues in General Creek and does not allow for adequate public safety access.

ProjectName: Tahoe City Gateway Trail Project
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Provide formal pedestrian and bike access to the extensive Burton Creek State Park trail system directly from Tahoe City and Tahoe State Recreation Area campground. Tie in with public transit and bike path. Phase 2 will include public Lake Tahoe overlook, picnic area, and pedestrian footpath.

ProjectName: Burton Creek SP Interpretive Prescribed Fire Management Trail Loop
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Showcase over 3 decades of prescribed fire management in different burn plots along a 2.5 mile loop trail system for public education and interpretation on using fire as an essential land management tool in this highly complex urban interface community. Project would include trail upgrades.

ProjectName: Burton Creek SP Access Bridge Replacement
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Goal is to upgrade emergency vehicle access and pedestrian bridge into Burton Creek State Park. Bridge requires replacement due to substantial ongoing erosion issues from the current undersized span over Burton Creek and inadequate size for fire response and public safety access.

ProjectName: Celio Barn Debris Removal and Meadow Restoration
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: This project proposes to remove hazardous debris from the dilapidated Celio Barn site in Washoe Meadows State Park and restore the natural hydrology and native meadow vegetation. Over the last decade, the barn has collapsed and scattered debris over a 925 square foot area. The barn site will be decompacted to allow native vegetation to grow and surface water to percolate. The STPUD service road has been improved to add water diversion features that will convey water towards the restored meadow site. In 2023, the California Conservation Corps spent 2 weeks removing dense pine growth to further encourage surface water, promote meadow habitat, and improve wildfire resilience.

ProjectName: Van Sickle Bi-State Park Phase 2
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
ProjectDescription: This project involves new park improvements at Van Sickle Bi-State Park.  Plans currently call for the construction of employee housing and a maintenance shop.   Employee housing will provide affordable housing to park employees and allow for rangers to be stationed onsite.  An improved maintenance facility will allow park staff to station maintenance personnel onsite.  The facilities will be utilized to support future developments at Van Sickle Bi-State Park.  Construction is anticipated to begin during the summer of 2026.

ProjectName: Dennis Machida Memorial Trail (Greenway Phase 1C)
ProjectDescription: This project is a continuation of multiple phases of the California Tahoe Conservancy's Greenway Multi-Use Trail Project.  This segment (1C) will provide for a multi-use paved trail from the easterly terminus of Phase 1A at Herbert Avenue, crossing into CTC-owned land connecting up and along Pioneer Trail right-of-way to the limits of Ski Run Boulevard.

ProjectName: Van Sickle Bi-State Park Phase 3
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
ProjectDescription: Van Sickle Phase 3 is an improvement to the Van Sickle Bi-State Park Phase 1.  Nevada State Parks has hired a contractor to design a visitor center, improved parking, and restrooms.  The visitor center will include park offices, a gift shop, and interpretive spaces.  A multi-use paved path is being planned from the visitor to the center to the state border.   The planning team is coordinating with California Tahoe Conservancy to continue the path to Lake Parkway.  An improved stateline monument is being planned for the Nevada/California Stateline that will include additional interpretive opportunities.   Construction is tentatively planned for the summer of 2026.

ProjectName: CSA #5 Erosion Control Project - Phase 3
ProjectDescription: The County Service Area (CSA) # 5 Erosion Control Project includes the developed portions of the northwest corner of the Tahoe Cedars subdivision southwest of Highway 89 between the El Dorado County line and Poplar Street. The Project implemented improvements to reduce the concentration of fine sediment in the storm water which exits the Project area before reaching Lake Tahoe. The Project was split into multiple phases. The final phase (Phase 3) project area is roughly bounded by Placer Street to the east, McKinney Street to the west, and the Placer/El Dorado County line to the north and west.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys East Channel Bubble Curtain
ProjectDescription: Bubble curtains are demonstrating the ability to restrict invasive aquatic plant fragment spread. A bubble curtain system has been installed in the East Channel of the Tahoe Keys to prevent plant fragments from leaving the East Channel and spreading to other areas of Lake Tahoe. The Tahoe Keys Marina is taking over responsibilities for its operation.

ProjectName: Stateline Avenue Complete Streets Project
ProjectDescription: The project seeks to rehabilitate Stateline Ave to provide safer pedestrian and bike access, lake access, and improved stormwater infrastructure. Informal dirt parking on shoulders and lack of sidewalk creates conflicts with pedestrians.  Informal dirt parking also generates sediment that runs off directly to the lake. The project looks to replace existing failing pipe with a new stormwater system that includes treatment while simultaneously addressing the unsecured shoulders. Constructing pedestrian and bike enhancements for the major tourist area is supported by The Tourist Core Area Plan. The project will be designed to connect to Park Ave, Lakeshore Blvd, and other regional connections.

ProjectName: Spruce and Blackwood Complete Streets Project
ProjectDescription: The project seeks to improve the multi-modal community access to the Bijou Community School.  Current issues of inadequate pedestrian accessibility and safety, poor drainage and water quality impacts from parking in the dirt would be addressed through new stormwater infrastructure coordinated with new pedestrian and cyclist safety and accessibility improvements. The project will incorporate and evaluate mobility improvements recommended in the LTUSD Safe Routes to School Master Plan. The project will seek to provide improvements along Spruce Avenue and Blackwood Road to provide increased safety and accessibility for pedestrians to connect to existing and future improvements in the area.

ProjectName: Park Avenue and Lakeshore Blvd Complete Streets
ProjectDescription: The Complete Streets project would improve the segment of Park Ave and Pine Blvd from Hwy 50 to Lakeshore Blvd to reduce flooding, address sediment from unsecured road shoulders, formalize parking, and improve accessibility and safety for pedestrians. The area has been identified as having drainage problems and lacking adequate pedestrian sidewalks, parking or streetscape elements. The rehabilitation of the roadways would include the construction of bike lanes, sidewalks, or shared use paths.

ProjectName: Fallen Leaf Road Rehabilitation Project
ProjectDescription: Fallen Leaf Road is ~5 miles in length from SR 89 to the south end of Fallen Leaf Lake at Stanford Sierra Camp.  The proposed project will complete roadway improvements in three phases: 1) SR89 to the Campground (0.6 miles); the Campground to Tahoe Mtn (1.8 miles), and Tahoe Mtn to Stanford Sierra Camp (2.9 miles).   Proposed improvements will include improving the pavement condition, eliminating substandard roadway geometry, and install drainage improvements to extend the service life of the roadway.  Widening of the roadway from SR 89 to the campground will be evaluated along with paving the existing roadway pullouts from the campground to Tahoe Mountain to improve the safety for all users

ProjectName: Ski Run Community Park
ProjectDescription:
Ski Run Community Park is South Lake Tahoe’s newest playground and community gathering space. The park is an example of what the community can accomplish to achieve a common goal to make Tahoe’s outdoor equitable for all.  
The Park includes an iconic 20-foot-tall rope climbing structure, accessible swing, hill slide, ski chair park benches donated by Heavenly Mountain Resort, play lawn, giant picnic table, and climbing boulder. The entire park was designed with accessibility in mind including an ADA parking space, accessible features, and bi-lingual signage. 

Ski Run Park opened in August 2024.

ProjectName: Aspen restoration in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
Jurisdiction: Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Carson City County, NV
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Tunnel Creek, Bonpland, Sand Harbor, Marlette Creek, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Glenbrook Creek, North Logan House Creek, Logan House Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Mcfaul Creek, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Trout Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Aspen stands in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park are at risk of being lost due to excessive conifer encroachment and other factors including defoliation by invasive White satin moths. This project seeks to restore aspen as the dominant tree in the forest canopy and stimulate regeneration in existing aspen stands. Restoration methods include conifer thinning and prescribed fire.

ProjectName: SR 28 North Parking, Sidewalk, and Water Quality Improvements
ProjectDescription: The SR28 North Parking, Sidewalk, and Water Quality Improvements includes environmental analysis, final design & construction of 30+ parking spaces (depending on design) north of the existing Tahoe Eastshore trailhead parking at Sweetwater Rd; build a connecting pedestrian path to the new Tahoe East Shore Trail connecting parking areas, 4-6 parking spaces at Rocky Point, address erosion and signage at Sunset Vista pullout, and 2-3 parking spaces for operational employee parking at the Tahoe Eastshore Trailhead, and water quality improvements within the existing NDOT Right of Way as part of the parking improvements. Once constructed, extend no parking zone from Ctry Club Dr to Sweetwater Rd.

ProjectName: SR 28 Central Corridor- Sand Harbor to Thunderbird Cove - Trail, Transit, and Safety Improvements
ProjectDescription: The project is located in Washoe County along SR 28, includes design and construction of 1.75 miles of multi-use path between Sand Harbor State Park and Thunderbird Cove, vista pullouts, and safety improvements.

ProjectName: Diamond Peak 25 Fuels Reduction Project
LeadImplementerName: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
ProjectDescription: This 46.8-acre project has completed fuels reduction treatments throughout the Diamond Peak Ski Resort. Most of the ski area has already been treated for fuels reduction through NLTFPD’s previous and on-going projects.  Neighboring property consists of USFS and private property. Funding has already been secured to reduce fuels on the USFS property and NLTFPD is also implementing treatments on the private property as part of their NV Regional Fuels Reduction Project. This project area is the final piece of the puzzle that will connect over 1,000 acres of contiguous hazardous fuels reduction treatments within the WUI Threat Zone of Incline Village.

ProjectName: North Lake Tahoe Defense Zone Improvement Project
LeadImplementerName: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
ProjectDescription: The North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District (NLTFPD) will reduce hazardous fuels on 210-620 acres and plan for additional hazardous fuels removal on federal and non-federal lands in the wildland-urban interface of Incline Village and Crystal Bay, NV to mitigate the wildfire risk to the community and improve forest health. The project will be accompanied by two public outreach activities that will showcase fuels reduction treatments and provide education on forest health, fuels treatments, and Fire Adapted Community concepts. These activities will create a better informed and more prepared Fire Adapted Community in Incline Village and Crystal Bay, NV, an area with extreme wildfire risk.

ProjectName: West Shore Water Storage Augmentation
ProjectDescription:
The Project will improve storage capacity to meet fire flows along the west shore of Lake Tahoe. The project will analyze the suitability of 4 water storage tanks, and associated transmission main layout within the TCPUD west shore service area to establish a common static hydraulic grade line, increasing storage capacity to meet fire flows.

Phase I is the construction of two new water tanks

ProjectName: TCPUD Fire Flow Capacity Improvements and Hydrant Installation, Phase I
ProjectDescription:
This Project provides improved fire flow capacity and fire hydrant coverage across the TCPUD water service areas. This phase occurs within the Dollar Point neighborhood, and will replace 1,500 linear feet of water mains and install additional 4 fire hydrants.

The objective is to improve water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage area.

ProjectName: TCPUD Lower Meeks Bay Water Pressure for Fire Flow
ProjectDescription: The Project consists of the installation of approximately 600 feet of new 8” water main and a pressure reducing valve station to connect the Meeks Bay Vista pressure zone to the Tahoe Hills distribution system. The system experiences severe head loss under fire flows. Providing a northernly connection will greatly improve fire flow at all hydrants along Meeks Bay Avenue and creates a redundant connection to the system in the event of a failure. Project improves water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage area.

ProjectName: Brockway Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
ProjectDescription: The water system is comprised of watermains ranging from 2 inches to 8 inches in diameter. The system is deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and does not meet current fire codes. The project would install 7,000 linear feet of new 8- and 10-inch diameter watermains to replace the existing less than 6-inch diameter watermains. Fifteen new fire hydrants would be installed that would be accessible from the public right of way.  The new upsized watermains would also improve flow capacity of the existing intertie with Incline Village GID which is limited to 200 gpm. Flow and pressure to customers would be improved for those served by the 2-inch backyard mains.

ProjectName: Trout Street Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Main water system in Kings Beach, CA was comprised of watermains ranging from 1- to 8- inches in diameter. The system was deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and did not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid.  The project installed 2,568 linear feet of new 8-inch watermain and 5 new fire hydrants on Trout and Brook Ave. to replace the existing 1- and 2-inch diameter steel watermain that serves the properties. Project improved water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage.

ProjectName: Post-Caldor Fire Stream Aggradation using Beaver Dam Analogues: Saxon and Trout Creeks
ProjectDescription: The watersheds within and downstream of the Caldor Fire Scar presented an opportunity to use the expected erosion from the landscape to promote channel aggradation within incised areas of the creeks. 80 BDAs were installed along Saxon and Trout Creeks, concentrated in areas that benefited from channel aggradation and riparian width expansion potential. Monitoring has shown a more dynamic channel morphology, increased aquatic species habitat complexity, channel aggradation, increased inset floodplains and improved floodplain connectivity. BDA projects can extend restoration efforts into remote areas where conventional projects would be cost prohibitive.

ProjectName: Community Watershed Planning Forest Health Implementation- North Shore
ProjectDescription: Work with private parcel owners to secure access to property and perform fuels management, stream restoration (handwork using downed timber or willow debris) and terrestrial invasive weed identification and removal. Funding will be pursued and project details developed.

ProjectName: Microplastics Beach Clean Up
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription:
The ECO-CLEAN Bot is an all-electric, solar + battery powered beach sifting robot that sifts and cleaners beaches without causing harmful degradation to the native flora and fauna. ECO-CLEAN BOT has the ability to clean over 3,000 sq/meters of beach per hour without emitting any fossil fuels. We feel this tool will remarkably change the way local agencies, jurisdictions, resorts and private residences clean their beaches. Removal of harmful macro plastics and debris is critical to preserving our natural wonders. 

ECO-CLEAN SOLUTIONS is proud to announce the deployment of the BEBOT Beach Cleaner in Lake Tahoe Summer 2022.

ProjectName: LTBMU Caldor Hazard Tree and Fuel Reduction Project
LeadImplementerName: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
ProjectDescription: Hazard tree removal and fuel reduction on approximately 1500 acres related to the Caldor Fire along roads, trails, adjacent to private property, and in developed sites.

ProjectName: LTBMU Caldor Restoration
LeadImplementerName: U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
ProjectDescription: Long term restoration of the Caldor Fire area within the Lake Tahoe Basin, including removal of fire-killed trees, fuels reduction, reforestation, trail restoration, and terrestrial and aquatic habitat restoration.

ProjectName: Crystal Peak Road - Watermain Replacement for Fire Protection
ProjectDescription: Replacement of 2300 linear feet of 6-inch water main with new 8-inch water main and increase quantities of fire hydrants to meet 2018 IFC code requirements. This project is a continuation of the multi-year program to replace 1960's era thin wall steel water mains and other deficient water mains. We also work closely with the North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District to determine areas of low fire flow, which may indicate a need for increased capacity in that area. Project improves water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage area.

ProjectName: STPUD Wastewater Treatment Plant Fuels Reduction project
ProjectDescription: South Tahoe Public Utility District treated 100 acres adjacent to the wastewater treatment facility with fuels reduction efforts.

ProjectName: Ralph Tank BMP and SEZ Restoration Project
ProjectDescription: Removal of water tank, associated structures and other coverage to access the facility located in SEZ near Bijou Creek. SEZ vegetation has been restored.    Parking barriers installed and water spreading BMPs in place on 2 parcels to permit foot access to remaining monitoring well facility.  4,428 sf total coverage removed & banked on APNs  025-551-006 & -007 as part of project.

ProjectName: Bowers/Bijou Area Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
ProjectDescription: STPUD deficiencies in fire flows and the number and spacing of fire hydrants did not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid. The Bowers/Bijou Area is located within the South Tahoe Public Utility District service area. The properties on the street are served by undersized water mains (2 to 4 inches in diameter) and cannot support fire hydrants adequately for required fire suppression. Additionally, the number and spacing of fire hydrants do not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid. These residential properties also have daily flow and pressure deficiencies. The project installed 10,400 feet of 8-inch water mains, improved system looping and added 15 new hydr

ProjectName: Black Bart Area Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
ProjectDescription:
The Black Bart Project installed 7,700 linear feet of new 6-inch water main to replace the existing 1- and 2-inch diameter steel water main that serves the properties. Nine new fire hydrants would be installed that would be accessible from the public right of way.
The project improves water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage area.

ProjectName: STPUD Fire Hydrant Upgrades and Improvements Fire Protection Project
ProjectDescription: STPUD updated, replaced, and/or installed 57 fire hydrants throughout its service area to reduce the current deficiencies in fire flow and available fire protection. The project will improve water supply by enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage areas.

ProjectName: Slott Peak Waterline  Improvements
ProjectDescription: Replacement of 330 linear feet of 6-inch water main with new 8-inch water main and replacement of one fire hydrant to meet NLTFPD code requirements. This project is a continuation of the multi-year program to replace 1960's era thin wall steel water mains and other deficient water mains. Replacement criteria is twofold: Replace those water mains with the most leaks and in streets with aging pavement. Since our water loss is now less than 6%, our main objective is to work closely with the Washoe County Road Department to replace water mains just prior to the County's repaving the street. Project  enhances fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands.

ProjectName: IVGID Fire Hydrant Replacement Program
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Tunnel Creek, Bonpland, Sand Harbor, Marlette Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Hundreds of fire hydrants within IVGID were installed >40years ago and are no longer in compliance with current NLTPFD adopted IFC code requirements and standard operating guidelines. The increasing age also means replacement parts are no longer available for certain manufacturer models. Replacement criteria is based on a priority basis determined cooperatively by IVGID and NLTFPD. The project aims to replace hydrants no longer suitable for continued maintenance and to modify hydrants that can be salvaged and updated to meet current code requirements. Project improves water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volum

ProjectName: Snowshoe Hare Resurvey
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
Jurisdiction: El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA
ProjectDescription: Resurvey J. Keane plots from the early 1990s focused on snowshoe hares. Keane PhD work was intended to assess changes in wildlife populations in response to forest management, particularly prescribed burning. Pilot project with field sampling by Tahoe Institute of Natural Sciences to inform larger scientific investigation.

ProjectName: Assessment of long term change in bird populations
LeadImplementerName: California Department of Parks and Recreation
ProjectDescription: Resurvey of John Keane PhD grid plots from the early 1990s to assess long term change in bird populations. The Keane PhD surveys were conducted for California State Parks to assess change in bird populations in response to forest management and prescribed fire. This survey work will be conducted by the Tahoe Institute for Natural Science.

ProjectName: Pioneer Trail/US Highway 50 Intersection Safety Improvement Project
ProjectDescription: This project aims to improve the intersection of US Highway 50/ State Route 89 and Pioneer Trail in the community of Meyers by replacing the existing signalized intersection with a modern roundabout. Once constructed features will include improving mobility, walkability, and sustainability of the intersection. Enhanced multimodal transportation improvements like visible crosswalks for bicycle and pedestrian movements, providing for future growth for transit facilities to enhance circulation and provide opportunities to experience Meyers as an active transportation user.

ProjectName: Burnt Cedar Beach - Lakeshore Blvd Stormwater BMPs
ProjectDescription:
IVGID’s Burnt Cedar property currently receives storm water that enters the property during precipitation and snowmelt events. This water enters the property through an 18-inch CMP culvert and comes exclusively from the Washoe County roadway swales. 
Currently, the only BMP is the grass area adjacent to the culvert. There are no permanent BMP’s to slow the stormwater and stop sediment from entering the lake. This also results in beach sections being washed out as the water flows down the property. IVGID proposes a permanent BMP system in which this storm water is controlled and will slow the rate of water allowing the sediment to drop out of the water prior to it entering the lake.

ProjectName: Incline Beach Stormwater Collection and BMP Improvements
ProjectDescription:
Incline Beach currently receives stormwater runoff from both Washoe County road facilities and the internal parking area for the Incline Beach. Existing SW channels are undersized and routinely are overwhelmed and eroded during large runoff events.
The Project proposes to improve the existing conveyance facilities channel  to reduce SW velocities and minimize erosion and sediment transport to Lake Tahoe.

ProjectName: Tahoe Rim Trail Visitor Use Monitoring Program
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: In 2022, the TRTA installed over 25 trail counters. These counters were placed on all nine Tahoe Rim Trail (TRT) segments and connector trails to better understand trail usage. All counters have been collected and data is currently being analyzed and compiled for reporting purposes. To supplement trail counter data, volunteers were also stationed at four different major trailheads of the TRT to collect data on the number of trail users that passed by on busy weekends and to determine day hiking or backcountry camping destinations. Additionally, a backcountry campsite inventory was performed at Star Lake and Showers Lake to better understand illegal camping impacts,

ProjectName: IVGID Rec Center Expansion
ProjectDescription: The proposed project is a 33,000 +/- sq. ft. expansion to the existing IVGID Rec Center. The expansion will include a new gymnasium, gymnastic facilities and storage, restrooms, multi-purpose and recreation rooms for youth programs, new entry and reception area and offices. Site improvements will include the installation of permanent BMPs, modified vehicle circulation for drop-off lane and parking.

ProjectName: Marlette Virtual Nature Trail
ProjectDescription: The Marlette Virtual Nature Trail follows 12 miles of existing trails from Spooner Lake to Tunnel Creek. The trail starts with a sign in the Spooner Lake parking area with instructions on how to access the trail information. A second sign is placed at the Tunnel Creek trailhead. The trail is hosted on the Google Earth platform, which offers Android and iPhone apps, as well as web-based maps. The trail follows the existing North Canyon, Marlette Flume, and Tunnel Creek trails. The trail has 20 points of interest highlighting plants, animals, geology, and human history such as Washoe culture and Comstock logging and mining.

ProjectName: Quantifying the status, trends, and demography of Tahoe draba (Draba asterophora), a Lake Tahoe Basin rare alpine plant
ProjectDescription: The alpine plant, Tahoe draba (Draba asterophora), is among the endemic plant species that occurs only in the Lake Tahoe region. We assess the status, long-term trends, and demographic vulnerabilities of Tahoe draba in the northern and southern Lake Tahoe Basin (LTB). To accomplish this, we: 1) Collate and digitize historic monitoring data of Tahoe draba populations; 2) Reestablish density and demographic monitoring transects of Tahoe draba in both its northern and southern LTB populations and monitor plants for 3 years; 3) Analyze current and historic data to quantify demographic rates, current status, and long-term trends of Tahoe draba in northern and southern populations.

ProjectName: Golden and Rainbow Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Main water system in Kings Beach, CA is deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and does not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid. This project installed 7,700 linear feet of new 8-inch watermain in Golden Ave., Rainbow Ave., and upper Secline Street to replace the existing 1- and 2-inch diameter steel watermain that served the properties. Twelve new fire hydrants have been installed that are accessible from the public right of way. The project improved water supply enhancing fire protection capabilities on private, local, state, and federal lands by increasing fire flow volumes and coverage.

ProjectName: Brook, Salmon, Yacht, and Dip Fire Protection Water Infrastructure
ProjectDescription: North Tahoe Public Utility District owns the Tahoe Main water system that serves the Kings Beach residential grid neighborhood. The water system is comprised of watermains ranging from 1- to 8- inches in diameter. The system is deficient in fire flows and in the number and spacing of fire hydrants and does not meet current fire codes on several streets in the grid. The project would install 2,650 linear feet of new 8-inch watermain on Brook, Salmon, Yacht, and Dip streets to replace the existing 1- and 2-inch diameter steel watermain that serves the properties. Five (5) new fire hydrants would be installed that would be accessible from the public right of way.

ProjectName: Restoring Lake Tahoe's Depths
Jurisdiction: Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Carson City County, NV
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Tunnel Creek, Bonpland, Sand Harbor, Marlette Creek, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Glenbrook Creek, North Logan House Creek, Logan House Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Mcfaul Creek, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Trout Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Restoring the Lake Depths Foundation is a Lake Tahoe based nonprofit. Rovers equipped with a gripper to remove trash are deployed and operated from boats. The rover continues to work diligently, removing a variety of plastics (before they become micro) and pollutants like cans with BPA's, tires and much more.

ProjectName: Y-Mobility Hub
ProjectDescription: The Y-Mobility Hub would provide multi-modal access to popular destinations within the City and Lake Tahoe beaches along the State Route 89 corridor north of the Y to facilitate other modes of transportation. The Mobility Hub would include a Park-n-Ride and facilities for fixed-route transit, micro transit and regional shuttle options to decrease dependency on private vehicles. The SR 89 corridor has multiple destinations and high visitation rates during peak season result in congestion and parking issues. East of Y on Highway 50 there is a need to connect people with residential and commercial areas along the Highway 50 corridor and the Stateline/Heavenly Village Tourist Core Area.

ProjectName: South Shore Microtransit Electrification
ProjectDescription: The City of South Lake Tahoe has partnered with the South Shore Transit Management Association to help facilitate the transition of the Lake Link microtransit fleet to electric. Dedicated overnight parking and Level 2 and Level 3 chargers are necessary to ensure success. The City has an aspirational goal to achieve 24/7 carbon free energy by 2030 and seeks to support Level 2 charging with with stored solar energy for overnight charging at a "Microtransit EV Charging Base Station".  The Level 3 charging will be for on-route charging as needed. The project takes an innovative technology approach to tracking carbon intensity of the fleet, a step toward 24/7 hourly certification.

ProjectName: Lake Link South Shore Microtransit
ProjectDescription: Microtransit service started on the South Shore July 2022 and expanded in January 2024. The South Shore Transit Management Association contracts with Downtowner to provide the Lake Link service, with free rides between any location in the service area. The expanded service area extends from Round Hill in Douglas county, NV to the Sierra Tract neighborhood the City of South Lake Tahoe, CA. The first year was a success, averaging over 10,000 riders per month. In the first month of expanded service, ridership increased 84% compared to 2023 with over 24,000 riders. ProjectDescription:
In 2021, Clean Up The Lake (CUTL) completed a nearshore (0 – 25 feet) lakebed litter cleanup along all 28 miles of Nevada’s Lake Tahoe shoreline. This effort removed 16,615 pieces of litter totaling 11,821 pounds.
In 2022 our team revisited 15 of these litter hotspot areas in Nevada, collecting 1,616.7 lbs of litter including 2,527 individual items. The findings suggest that the initial 72 mile cleaning was highly effective at removing the majority of lakebed litter. Litter collected for the first time from sites at depth 35ft and 70ft appeared in the same proportions as litter collected from the nearshore. This suggest that litter is likely being transported from nearshore to depth.

ProjectName: Spooner Meadow Restoration Project
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Lands
ProjectDescription: Spooner Meadow is an important ecosystem along Tahoe’s east shore. It provides cover, perennial water, and food resources for over one hundred species of wildlife. Historical water channelization, grazing, logging, and a lack of natural fire events have reduced its capacity to function as a normal, healthy meadow ecosystem. Climate change threatens to eliminate Tahoe’s meadows via reduced snowpacks, declining groundwater, and warmer temperatures. Restoration of Spooner Meadow would maintain its role as a vital wildlife nesting and migration corridor. Restoration will involve Nevada Division of State Parks in order to balance natural resource objectives with recreational opportunities.

ProjectName: Land Tender Tahoe Stewardship Atlas and Beta Program
ProjectDescription: To address the complex challenges in collaborative forest management, Vibrant Planet created Land Tender, a cloud based visual scenario-building and decision support application for accelerated forest management planning and disturbance risk mitigation in wildland-connected communities. The Tahoe Stewardship Atlas is a dynamic map of ecologically based landscape segments containing the appraised values and risks of assets and resources located within these segments, as well as the estimated return on investment from forest treatment projects. With the California Tahoe Conservancy and the Tahoe Fund, we generated a comprehensive treatment plan for the entire 205,000-acre Tahoe Basin.

ProjectName: HWY 50 Fuel Reduction
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat between 90 to 115 acres of forestland within the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) along the US Highway 50 corridor between Glenbrook and Zephyr Cove, NV. This treatment will help to modify potential fire behavior such that firefighters will be able to safely protect life, property, and the environment from an approaching wildland fire. This project will also drastically increase the sustainability of the ecosystems by returning the environment back to a more “natural” landscape in terms of vegetation/tree density and species composition. Treatment will include thinning and removal of fuels within the project areas.

ProjectName: Cattlemans/Black Bart Retrofit Project
ProjectDescription: The Cattlemans and Black Bart Basins were constructed as part of the Pioneer Trail III Erosion Control Project in 2001.  The improvements included corrugated steel pipe outlet structures with atrium racks near the edge of the basin side slopes.  Since construction the basins have become wet basins with the outlet structures now under water most of the year.  The 2025 project focused on retrofit of the outlet pipes so as discharge runoff above the existing basin surface water elevations allowing for proper inspections and maintenance related to runoff and sediment transport.

ProjectName: Lahontan Cutthroat Trout fish planting in Echo Lake and Sawmill Pond
ProjectDescription: Annual fish planting in Echo lake and Sawmill Pond. Organization of a family fishing event at Sawmill pond each summer.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Fragment Containment
ProjectDescription:
Containment of aquatic invasive plant fragments in the Tahoe Keys is a high priority for AIS Program partners as the Tahoe Keys are the main source of AIP to the rest of the lake. Partners are coming together to implement and guide innovative and diverse containment practices, described in the Containment Plan (see link). The collaborative includes the Tahoe Keys Marina, the Tahoe Keys Property Owners Association, Keep Tahoe Blue, TRPA, Tahoe RCD, EcoClean Solutions, Marine Taxonomic Services, Inventive Resources Inc, US Forest Service, and Lahontan. 
Efforts will be monitored and reported each season while a holistic long-term plan for control of the Tahoe Keys is developed.

ProjectName: Edgewood Creek Restoration & Forest Health Project within TRPA/NDOT parcels
ProjectDescription: This project along Kingsbury Grade/SR207 within Douglas County proposes to perform fuels reduction and restore a portion of Edgewood Creek to improve stream function and water quality, along with improving the stormwater treatment directly connected to Edgewood creek via the TRPA treatment BMPs. Specifically (1) Capture and treat TRPA stormwater runoff prior to entering Edgewood Creek by improving treatment BMPs. (2) Remove unnecessary fill and restore the channel of Edgewood Creek. (3) Perform fuels reduction throughout the entire project area, but specifically within the SEZ. (4) Prevent, control, or eradicate terrestrial invasive species.

ProjectName: Lake Tahoe East Shore Asian Clam and Metaphyton Delineation and Control
LeadImplementerName: UC Davis Tahoe Environmental Research Center
ProjectDescription: The expanse of non-native Asian clam populations with the concurrent appearance of metaphyton (unattached algae) along Lake Tahoe’s east shore beaches has become an increasing concern. Due to the high nutrient concentrations from clam excretions and their stimulatory effect on algal growth, nuisance algae is starting to accumulate underwater and on beaches having negative aesthetic impacts. Five beaches were surveyed in summer 2023, using SCUBA and UAV imagery, to delineate the extent and density of Asian clams and any associated metaphyton growth. A metaphyton removal pilot study to determine the effectiveness of removing metaphyton algae before contaminating beaches was conducted.

ProjectDescription: This project assesses the impact of the smoke and ash from the 2021 Caldor Fire on stormwater quality.  Urban stormwater runoff samples were taken during and immediately after the active burn period and analyzed for markers associated with smoke and ash. Elevated concentrations of several of these markers were found in samples taken during the active burn period, but dropped off quickly as the fire was contained. This indicates that the Caldor Fire had a relatively transitory impact on urban stormwater quality, but likely delivered pollutants to Lake Tahoe, contributing to changes documented by rapid-response investigations on lake ecology and aquatic conditions before and after the fire.

ProjectName: Skyland Shaded Fuel Break
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat approximately 17 acres of US Forest Service lands to the South and East of the Skyland community.  Treatment will consist of hand treatment and forest fuels mastication to create a “Shaded Fuel Break” as defined by the National Wildfire Coordinating Group; Fuel breaks built in timbered areas where the trees on the break are thinned and pruned to reduce the fire potential yet retain enough crown canopy to make a less favorable microclimate for surface fires.

ProjectName: Spooner Lake and Backcountry State Park Trail Plan
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
ProjectDescription: This project will update the  parks' master plan for the park.  The primary goal of this project is to move non-motorized users off the parks service roads and improve connectivity to the backcountry trail system.  A planning firm will be utilized to complete a resource assessment of the project area.   The resource assessment will identify wildlife, water quality, forest health, and historical resource concerns. The team will utilize the resource assessment to identify possible trail corridors for trail construction or improvements.  New trail corridors that meet the project goal will then receive further environmental review and trail construction documents will be produced.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Lagoons Long Term Water Quality Improvement Project Planning
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys POA is planning, addressing technical issues, and engaging stakeholders to identify actions to improve the long-term quality and beneficial uses of waters of the Tahoe Keys Lagoons (i.e., the Marina, West, and Lake Tallac lagoons).   Existing condition evaluations are focusing on non-point sources of nutrients.  Future evaluations will include:  1) nutrient inputs from upgradient shallow groundwater and surface sources internal to the lagoons, 2) methods to improve the lagoons circulation and reduce algae/HABs, 3) Lake Tallac Lagoon outflow effects on Pope Marsh, 4) lagoons organic sediment nutrient contributions to water quality, and 5) possible mitigations for climate change

ProjectName: Zooplankton Ecology of Lake Tahoe
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription: The project team filled key knowledge gaps by (1) quantifying the horizontal and vertical distribution of zooplankton across the spatial extent of Lake Tahoe, (2) determining the composition and amount of microzooplankton, and (3) quantifying the role of nearshore and offshore zooplankton communities on particle size distribution in their respective habitats. The data generated from this project is available to public, management, and scientific communities for evaluation so others can use the data and contribute to our understanding on how to better conserve Lake Tahoe.

ProjectName: Characteristics, Composition, and Relative Sources of Particles Affecting Lake Tahoe Water Clarity
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription:
This project assessed the composition, relative concentrations, and contributing source of particles in runoff and in the lake. The products will further inform clarity model development and will contribute to improved linkages between watershed, nearshore, and lake processes. Results include:
•	The study provides a new way to “fingerprint” the particles that reduce clarity, allowing managers to distinguish urban runoff particles from natural watershed and in-lake sources.
•	The findings reaffirm that urban stormwater is a distinct clarity problem, not just a larger share of sediment.
•	The project provides novel methods to help separate external loading from in-lake processes.

ProjectDescription: Wildlands Network and Pathways for Wildlife are conducting a wildlife connectivity study throughout the Tahoe Basin. Funded by the California Tahoe Conservancy, this multifaceted study will utilize GIS modeling, conduct an extensive camera survey, and collect roadkill data to identify where and how wildlife are moving throughout the Basin. By collecting this data, we will be able to understand where there are bottlenecks and barriers to movement and where land management enhancements can be made to improve wildlife connectivity.  Ultimately, this study will inform land managers where there are critical areas for wildlife and potential locations for wildlife crossing infrastructure.
