ProjectDescription: Tahoe Conservancy's Tahoe for All Grant Program supports programs and projects that remove or reduce barriers for underserved people to access Lake Tahoe's outdoor recreation destinations. The Conservancy funded four projects in 2022 and another four in 2023. In 2025, the Conservancy opened another funding round and anticipates awarding grants in March 2026. More information on the program can be found here: https://tahoe.ca.gov/tahoe-for-all-grants/

ProjectName: Picnic Area and Lake Access Improvements at Patton Landing Beach
ProjectDescription: The Conservancy will construct improvements at Patton Landing Beach to improve picnic areas, paths of travel, and lake access so that all people can better utilize the facility and the lake access it provides. Improvements include resurfacing walkways, providing accessible paths to the lake shore, installing accessible picnic areas and tables, and improving restroom facilities.

ProjectName: Picnic and Lake Access Improvements at North Tahoe Beach
ProjectDescription: The Conservancy will construct improvements at North Tahoe Beach to improve picnic areas, paths of travel, restrooms, and lake access so that all people can better utilize the facility and the lake access it provides. Improvements include resurfacing walkways, providing accessible paths to the lake shore, installing accessible picnic areas and tables, and improving restroom facilities.

ProjectName: Picnic and Lake Access Improvements at Carnelian West Beach
ProjectDescription: The Conservancy will construct improvements at Carnelian West Beach to improve picnic areas, paths of travel, restrooms, and lake access so that all people can better utilize the facility and the lake access it provides. Improvements include resurfacing walkways, providing accessible paths to the lake shore, installing accessible picnic areas and tables, and improving restroom facilities.

ProjectName: Upper Truckee Restoration Bird and Bumble Bee monitoring
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, El Dorado County, CA, Alpine County
ProjectDescription: The Institute for Bird Populations (IBP) will provide long-term monitoring of overall bird abundance, community composition, and habitat composition, and bumble bee abundance, community composition, and habitat composition for meadow systems throughout the lower reaches of the Upper Truckee River and nearby tributaries to Lake Tahoe, in El Dorado County, CA. Study sites will include those known locally as the Upper Truckee Marsh, Johnson Meadow, Reaches 5 and 6, Golf Course, Trout Creek, Cold Creek Meadow, and at a nearby control site, Angora Creek.

ProjectName: Emerald Bay Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
ProjectDescription: Emerald Bay is one of the most successful aquatic invasive plant (AIP) control treatments completed to date by the Lake Tahoe AIS program. Zero to few aquatic invasive plants had been detected since 2014, until recent surveillance monitoring in 2022 revealed AIP that required a higher level of work that was no longer considered a rapid response action. Dedicated treatment includes diver-assisted suction removal and hand-pulling. To ensure the long-term effectiveness of this work, routine surveillance monitoring is occuring, and training of California Department of State Parks divers to conduct annual monitoring and removal of any emerging aquatic invasive plants.

ProjectName: Sand Harbor State Park Master Plan Update
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
ProjectDescription: The current Sand Harbor layout was designed in 1970 and improperly designed for the current visitation.  This project updates the 1990 master plan for the park and create a sustainable vision for the future of Sand Harbor.  The master plan will then be implemented in a series of EIP projects to improve traffic flow, recreation experience, and sustainability of the site.

ProjectName: New Zealand Mudsnail Rapid Response
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: On 9/6/2023, invasive New Zealand mudsnails (NZMS) were discovered in areas off the South Shore by divers conducting aquatic invasive plant monitoring. Following rapid response protocols under the federally approved Lake Tahoe Aquatic Invasive Species Management Plan, TRPA convened an incident team comprised of staff from TRPA, Tahoe RCD, and partner experts and began rapid response actions: delineation, tracking spread, updating prevention procedures, expanded outreach and education, and researching management options. A technical advisory committee was formed to provide expertise. Actions to track and prevent spread have been incorporated into AIS program protocols.

ProjectName: Pilot project: Sonar Methods for Aquatic Plant Monitoring
ProjectDescription: Pilot project to better understand capabilities of sonar to enhance monitoring of aquatic invasive plant infestations. Methods include multibeam, side scan, dual frequency sonar, and comparison of commercially available sonar software.

ProjectName: Washoe Tribe of Nevada & California Engagement and Capacity
LeadImplementerName: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California
ProjectDescription: The Washoe Tribe of Nevada & California has received a grant through the California Tahoe Conservancy so the Tribe can build the capacity of our Tribal program in staying engaged with environmental partners in basin, obtain the training and guidance necessary to carry out cultural burns on Tribal land, as well as non-tribal where approved. Another portion of the grant is to increase the capacity and production of our cultural greenhouse where we are planting pinyon pine, sage brush, and other culturally significant plants to the Washoe Tribe. The plants will be used for meadow, and forest restoration on the Tribe's aboriginal lands.

ProjectName: Lake Valley Fire Protection District Capacity Planning Project
ProjectDescription: The LVFPD will be responsible for planning and preparing for the implementation of high priority fuels reduction and wildfire prevention projects on state, local government, and private lands in the South Shore area of the Lake Tahoe Basin (Basin). This work will be done in coordination with the Conservancy, the Tahoe Fire and Fuels Team (TFFT), the Tahoe Resource Conservation District, and other Basin partners. Once implemented, the fuels reduction and wildfire prevention projects will help to restore the resilience of Basin forests and watersheds, foster Basin-wide climate change adaption, reduce fire risk for communities, and increase the capacity for planning and implementing projects.

ProjectName: Stormwater Management Tools for the Lake Tahoe Basin
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: The project will update the Pollutant Load Reduction Model (PLRM) and the Regional Stormwater Monitoring Program Data Management System (RSWMP-DMS) to align with modern computing platforms and develop a program for sustaining continued improvements, enhanced utility, and easier maintenance. Software updates will maintain current functionality and fix lingering bugs in both systems. PLRM improvements will allow for users to run the PLRM with more current precipitation data, discrete storm event data, and predicted future climate data to be used for project planning. DMS improvements will enhance analysis and reporting to better represent impacts of urban runoff loads to Lake Tahoe.

ProjectName: Logan Shoals Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
ProjectDescription: Aquatic invasive plant removal implemented at Logan Shoals is prioritized in the Action Agenda, a multi-year lake-wide strategy to remove aquatic invasive plants along the shoreline of Lake Tahoe. Methods of removal included barrier installation, diver-assisted suction (if needed), and hand removal. Barriers were installed at this site in 2023 and removed in 2024. Divers continued surveillance monitoring at this site throughout the 2024 and 2025 plant growing seasons. Future reporting for this project will be documented in Project # 01.03.01.0037 Lake-wide Surveillance and Site Assessments.

ProjectName: Wovoka Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
ProjectDescription: In October 2022 during a surveillance monitoring survey, a dense Eurasian watermilfoil infestation was observed by divers. In 2023, Tahoe RCD's contracted dive team installed barriers in June to control Eurasian watermilfoil. Barriers were removed in November 2023, and follow-up surveys and  plant removal continued in 2024. Due to successful diver removal efforts and minimal detection of newly rooted Eurasian watermilfoil during surveillance visits in 2024, this project has reached post-implementation surveillance status. All future surveillance visits will be documented in Project # 01.03.01.0037 Lake-wide Surveillance and Site Assessments.

ProjectName: Corridor Coordination
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County

ProjectDescription: This project proposes support for corridor coordination regarding necessary project agreements, MOU's, financing and funding, planning, design, implementation and post construction operations and maintenance activities across multiple jurisdictions, partner and land management agencies to streamline the delivery process of large scale corridor based projects.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Lagoons (Entirety) Aquatic Invasive Weed Control Planning
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys is the highest priority location of invasive aquatic weed control. With the completion of the Tahoe Keys Control Methods Test, data collected will inform a holistic treatment regime for the entirety of the Tahoe Keys. Maximizing fragment containment and interim treatments will take place in 2025, as well as stakeholder engagement. Planning and environmental review will be the next step planning to solve this complicated infestation.

ProjectName: Terrace View Sewer Line Burke Headwaters Restoration
ProjectDescription: Between Terrace View and N. Benjamin Road, there is an export sewer line under a branch of Burke Creek that will be relocated out of the stream zone as part of its life span replacement. This project proposes to restore the SEZ that has been impaired by the dirt sewer line access road and trails.

ProjectName: Burke Creek Rabe Meadow Upper Meadows Restoration and Pump Station Road Realignment
ProjectDescription: This project achieves items that were not covered in the Burke Creek Rabe Meadow Riparian Restoration and includes trail realignments out of riparian areas, filling of ditches that drain meadows, removal of conifers that encroach on meadows, and the construction of a new access in higher capability land for the existing sewer pump station on NV Beach.

ProjectName: Rabe Meadow Drought and Climate Resilience Project
ProjectDescription: There are 2 ephemeral drainages that flow into the existing Douglas County Lake Tahoe Sewer Authority (DCLTSA) emergency overflow pond. Per their NDEP permit, this clean water is pumped out to be treated at the sewer plant and then exported over the hill. These natural drainages should be flowing into Rabe Meadow as spring runoff and will help with water quantity in drought years. This project establish flow paths and SEZ areas around the existing DCLTSA emergency overflow pond and this water will eventually reach Rabe Meadow.

ProjectName: Purchase of Two XBroom Street Sweepers
Watershed: Bijou Park, Bijou Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Purchase of two 2023 Freightliner CNG Chassis with mounted XBroom  to replace two failing units. Project requests $405,601 in O&M Funds. O&M Funds matched with $405,601 in City of South Lake Tahoe General Funds. The cost of each unit is approximately $405,601 which totals to $811,202 for two units.

ProjectName: TCPUD Multi-Use Trail System Reconstruction and Safety Enhancement Project
ProjectDescription:
Trail reconstruction and safety improvements for 13.1 miles of multi-use trail. The project will be completed in seven phases.

2024 - North Shore Trail
2025 - West Shore Trail Segments 2 & 3 (Sunnyside to Idlewild Way)
2026 - West Shore Trail Segment 1 (64 Acres to Sunnyside)
2028 - West Shore Trail Segment 4
2030 - West Shore Trail Segment 5

ProjectName: Echo Lake 2023- Pilot Underwater SCUBA Litter Clean Up
ProjectDescription: In the Echo Lake Pilot Research project, the team conduct a comprehensive assessment of the factors threatening Echo Lake’s health as well as remove litter. The findings of this project suggest that for Echo Lake, there is a low urgency for a full circumnavigated cleanup which are typically recommended for lakes that rank medium to high urgency as they allow our teams to address the heavily littered lake beds. Our organization was encouraged by the result of the pilot research that indicated lower levels of litter accumulation in Echo Lake.

ProjectName: Airport Fuel Reduction
ProjectDescription: Fuels reduction pile burning to reduce fuel loading around airport property

ProjectName: Spooner Lake Phase 3
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
ProjectDescription: The Spooner Lake Front Country Phase III project includes a new lake viewing platform and a non-motorized boat launch to provide high quality visitor services at Spooner Lake in Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park.  The Non-Motorized Boat Launch will be a concrete ramp that begins above the high-water mark and curves into the lake following the natural contour of the lake bottom. The Lake Viewing Platform is an elevated walkway leading to a square or rectangular platform with benches, supported by piers.

ProjectName: South Tahoe Refuse Wood Energy
ProjectDescription: South Tahoe Refuse & Recycling (STR) is exploring the installation of a 125-250kW wood waste gasifier at its South Lake Tahoe facility. Gasification has been around since the early 1800’s – instead of burning, chemical reactions turn the green waste into a gas that is a cleaner substitute for fossil fuels. If installed, the net metering system would offset the majority of grid electricity and natural gas used at the STR site by using 10-15% of the wood waste currently collected by STR, and reduce traffic and emissions from transporting waste material out of the Basin by over 70 truckloads each year.

ProjectDescription: The Washoe Tribe Prescribed Fire Training Exchange (TREX) is a dynamic effort that combines indigenous knowledge, community collaboration, and modern land management techniques to address several interconnected goals crucial for the well-being of the environment, culture, and Washoe Tribal communities.

ProjectName: Tahoe Fire and Fuels Team Coordinator and Capacity Building
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County

ProjectDescription: This project is intended to build capacity and support for the Basin-wide Tahoe Fire and Fuels Team (TFFT) by providing a full-time TFFT Program coordinator. The TFFT is based on partner participation and has seen better success when there is a dedicated coordinator. The TFFT Coordinator will provide full-time, focused support to the TFFT and its members. The TFFT Coordinator will work under the direction of the TFFT Incident Commander, coordinate and facilitate meetings, prepare and deliver grant proposals for member agencies, be the liaison to the Multi-Agency Coordinating Committee (MAC), and maintain TFFT project data including updating the Lake Tahoe EIP Project Tracker.

ProjectName: Washoe Meadows State Park and Lake Valley State Recreation Area WUI Hazardous Fuels Reduction - Planning
ProjectDescription: Washoe Meadows State Park and Lake Valley State Recreation Area WUI Hazardous Fuels Reduction - Planning Project will address the long term program of forest management and fuel reduction on state lands in South Lake Tahoe. The primary objective of the project is to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires that could damage Lake Tahoe Basin forests, watersheds, habitats, and communities and increase the pace and scale of fuel reduction in the park and recreation area. Once completed, state implementers can efficiently and comprehensively evaluate the effects of forest management, and improve the project approval and delivery process for subsequent activities.

ProjectName: Secline Beach Enhancement Project
ProjectDescription: The NTPUD, CTC, and Placer County are working together to improve Secline Beach in Kings Beach, California. Phase I includes community outreach, a needs assessment, and the development of conceptual improvement plans. Possible improvements to Secline Beach area include the construction of new public restrooms, formal picnic areas, organized kayak and paddleboard storage, e-bike and electric vehicle charging stations, and coordinated public transportation for beach visitors.  Additional public access enhancements could also include walkable connections to the nearby North Tahoe Beach and Kings Beach State Recreation Area, as outlined in the current Tahoe Basin Area Plan.

ProjectName: Truckee-Tahoe Regional BurnBot Pilot
LeadImplementerName: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
ProjectDescription:
A broad coalition of stakeholders, including the Tahoe Fund, North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District, Tahoe Fire & Fuels Team, Martis Fund, and the Tahoe Truckee Community Foundation, are bringing BurnBot to Tahoe to pilot and showcase its potential to help increase the pace and scale of forest health treatments safely and effectively. 

We hope this two-part pilot will lead to the incorporation of BurnBot into our regional forest health and wildfire prevention strategy. BurnBot provides remote-operated, tech-driven systems for both mastication and prescribed burns that make each process faster, safer and easier to carry out.

ProjectName: SR 267 Roadway Rehabilitation
ProjectDescription:
Near Truckee, from Nevada County line to Dolly Varden Avenue.  Rehabilitate pavement and drainage systems, upgrade guardrail and facilities to Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards, and extend southbound truck climbing lane. (PM 0.0 to PM 9.63)  EA 2J190

The Tahoe basin portion of the project will install bike route signage and striping from Carnelian Bay Ave to PM 9.63.

ProjectName: South Lake Tahoe Chipping Program
Watershed: Mckinney Creek, General Creek, Meeks Creek, Sierra Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: The South Lake Chipping Program unites residents in a collaborative effort to mitigate wildfire risks and enhance the safety of our community. By participating in the program, individuals have the opportunity to proactively clear vegetation around their properties, creating defensible spaces that protect homes and neighborhoods from the threat of wildfires. With a focus on sustainability and community engagement, the chipped materials are repurposed for landscaping projects, promoting environmental stewardship and minimizing waste. Through the Chipping Program, residents not only contribute to a safer and more resilient community but also foster a sense of unity and shared responsibility.

ProjectName: Dennis T. Machida Memorial Greenway (Phase 3)
ProjectDescription: The Dennis T. Machida Memorial Greenway Phase 3 project would extend this Class 1 shared-use trail from Ski Run Boulevard to Van Sickle Bi-State Park.

ProjectName: SLT Bikeway Realignment and Restoration at Link Road
ProjectDescription: Relocate a section of the South Lake Tahoe Bikeway out of the Upper Truckee Marsh and into the adjacent uplands in the vicinity of Link Road and create a direct connection to Sussex Avenue. This project will allow for significant SEZ and Wetland restoration and formalize a heavily trafficked native surface route that is much more direct. The existing alignment was intended to be temporary until acquisitions were completed.

ProjectName: SR 28 South Corridor Secret Harbor to Spooner
ProjectDescription: Five miles of East Shore Trail and 40 parking spaces at Skunk Harbor.

ProjectName: Kingsbury Shaded Fuel Break
ProjectDescription:
The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat approximately 16 acres of US Forest Service lands of the Upper Kingsbury Area to the East of Andria Street . Treatment will consist of hand treatment, prescribed burning, and forest fuels mastication to create a “Shaded Fuel Break” as defined by the National Wildfire Coordinating Group; Fuel breaks built in timbered areas where the trees and brush on the break are thinned and pruned to reduce the fire potential yet retain enough crown canopy to make a less favorable microclimate for surface fires.

Reporting for this project is under 02.01.01.0097 - Urban Forest Defense Zone Fuels Reduction and Healthy Forest Project

ProjectName: Lower Kingsbury Shaded Fuel Break
ProjectDescription:
The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat approximately 12 acres of US Forest Service lands to the North of the Lower Kingsbury community. Treatment will consist of hand treatment, prescribed burning, and forest fuels mastication to create a “Shaded Fuel Break” as defined by the National Wildfire Coordinating Group; Fuel breaks built in timbered areas where the trees on the break are thinned and pruned to reduce the fire potential yet retain enough crown canopy to make a less favorable microclimate for surface fires.
Project Accomplishments are reported in LTBMU project 02.01.01.0097 - Urban Forest Defense Zone Fuels Reduction and Healthy Forest Project

ProjectName: Homewood Forest Fuels Reduction Project
ProjectDescription: The project includes forest fuels removal over 252 acres to improve forest stand conditions and overall forest health. The selection tree removal will target the removal of suppressed, dead, dying, and non-resilient stands of timber for forest health and risk reduction of catastrophic wildfire. The objective of the timber harvesting is to improve the remnant stands of forest and timber to a healthy and desirable physiological condition promoting forest resilience and the desired phenology throughout the area and to bolster public safety from severe wildfire.

ProjectName: Mutushahoo Watah: Trout Creek Meadow Restoration
ProjectDescription: The Lake Tahoe Community College is interested in reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfire, improving hydrologic function, and restoring lost habitat in the Trout Creek Meadow between Hwy 50 and Martin Ave. Ecosystem restoration will include the removal of ~20 acres of lodgepole pine that have encroached upon the meadow surface and the use of traditional ecologic knowledge and cultural burning practices. This project is part a larger effort to reconnect Indigenous Communities with the landscape and increase the diversity of native plants, habitat, & culturally significant species.

ProjectName: PROTECT - Resilience Improvement Plan and Regional Emergency Communications/Transportation Plan
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County

ProjectDescription: A PROTECT Grant was awarded to TRPA from the FHWA in 2024. This grant will support the development of a Resilience Improvement Plan that assesses the Basin's transportation system’s vulnerabilities in the face of wildfires, extreme winter weather events and other natural hazards. The project also will assess necessary upgrades to the region’s communications infrastructure to ensure that transportation and utility entities, fire service, law enforcement, environmental organizations and community-based groups can benefit from an integrated, efficient, safe evacuation during emergencies.

ProjectName: SR 89/California State Park Rd Pedestrian Improvement Project (SHOPP Minor B)
ProjectDescription: Near Tahoma, 0.1 mile north of California State Park Road (PM 26.119). Install Rectangular Rapid Flash Beacons (RRFBs).  EA 0N920

Watershed: Bijou Park, Bijou Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Fuels Reduction Projects for SLT Airport grounds, Tahoe Island and the 56 acre campground by the lake locations to increase community wildfire protection and forest resilience. Focus for the projects is to reduce the fuel loading and provide for forest restoration.

ProjectName: South Lake Tahoe SNPLMA R18 Fuels Reduction Project Campground Recreation
ProjectDescription:
Fuels Reduction Projects for 56 Acre area to increase community wildfire protection and forest resilience. Focus for the projects is to reduce the fuel loading and provide for forest restoration. Terminating this project and including all three as part of a single SNPLMA funded project for the three areas.

This project is being combined with the other SNPLMA Round 18 projects and reported under 02.01.02.0023 - South Lake Tahoe SNPLMA R18 Fuels Reduction Airport Project.

ProjectName: South Lake Tahoe SNPLMA R18 Fuels Reduction Project Tahoe Vista
ProjectDescription:
Fuels Reduction Projects for SLT Tahoe Vista grounds to increase community wildfire protection and forest resilience. Focus for the projects is to reduce the fuel loading and provide for forest restoration.

This project is being combined with the other SNPLMA Round 18 projects and reported under 02.01.02.0023 - South Lake Tahoe SNPLMA R18 Fuels Reduction Airport Project.

ProjectName: Tahoe Truckee Airport District/ North Tahoe Fire-  River Road Project 1
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Truckee Airport District - North Tahoe Fire (TTAD/NTF) River Road Fuels Reduction Project 1 is located on the south side of the Highway 89 corridor where it parallels the Truckee River between Tahoe City and Alpine Meadows, CA. This portion of Highway 89 is a primary evacuation route for Lake Tahoe residents and visitors and it is within the Defense Zone of the Wildland Urban Interface. The project addresses dead and dying trees, ladder fuels, and excessive ground fuels and will be part of a series of projects to reduce hazardous fuels and improve forest health, allowing for the highway corridor to better serve for evacuation among multiple benefits.

ProjectName: Regan Beach Enhancement and Accessibility Improvement Project
ProjectDescription: The project will focus on a crucial segment of Phase 1, known as Regan Landing, to enhance both access and user experience. Planned improvements include creating a more welcoming pedestrian zone with upgraded pathways, redesigning the drop-off area for smoother vehicle access and safety, and enhancing ADA-compliant features. Additionally, the project will install new restrooms and a concession stand, establish designated picnic and barbecue areas with fixed seating, and provide SUP rental storage for residents. Landscaping enhancements will further beautify the park and promote a more sustainable environment.

ProjectName: Edgewood Properties Fuel Reduction
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District will treat approximately 15 acres of private lands East of the Hwy 50 corridor and West of the Bi-State Van Sickle State Park.

ProjectName: Nevada Understory Burning Program
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry

Some of the project area will be a reburn from 10 years ago, while other project areas will see the first reintroduction of  beneficial fire in over 100 years. These forests historically burned every 5-20 years, and are long overdue for understory burning.

ProjectDescription: Whitebark pine (Pinus albicaulis) is a federally threatened conifer that grows in mixed conifer and subalpine forests across western North America. It provides high value wildlife habitat, modulates spring runoff, and stabilizes slopes. Threats include climate change, wildfire, mountain pine beetle outbreaks, and white pine blister rust. Collection of cones from apparent blister rust resistance trees is needed to screen for blister rust resistance and identify future operational cone collection trees. This project would involve cone production surveys, cone caging, and cone collection. Cones would subsequently be sent to USFS Nursery Facility to conduct white pine blister rust screening.

ProjectName: FlyTahoe: Cross-Lake Electric Flying Ferry - Ride the Future
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV
ProjectDescription: FlyTahoe, America’s first electric flying ferry, will halve travel times for the 20,000 daily drivers between North and South Tahoe. By providing a cleaner, faster alternative to driving, our silent cross-lake service will reduce traffic congestion and automobile dependency while eliminating emissions and road sediment, preserving the lake’s clarity and better linking Tahoe’s communities. See it in action in Sweden at flytahoe.com. With 10x operational efficiency gains from electric hydrofoils, our model will unlock profitability while making flying across the lake cheaper than driving around it. By flying above the waves with no wake, FlyTahoe will cause no seasickness or shoreline erosion.

ProjectName: North Lake Tahoe Regional Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory
Watershed: Griff Creek, Tahoe Vista, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Carnelian Bay Creek, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Lake Forest Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Blackwood Creek, Eagle Rock, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, General Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: The Project will provide Tahoe City Public Utility District (TCPUD) and North Tahoe Public Utility District (NTPUD) an opportunity to understand a comprehensive view of operations emissions, manage Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions output, identify opportunities to reduce GHG emissions, and measure progress toward local, regional, state, and federal climate goals. The objective is to create a baseline and current year GHG Inventory for the North Lake Tahoe region from state line at Crystal Bay west to the Nevada County line and south along the west shore to Emerald Bay. The inventory includes data on emissions from services provided by the TCPUD and the NTPUD within their service territories.

ProjectName: Tunnel Creek Hazardous Fuels Reduction Project
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of Forestry
ProjectDescription: Tunnel Creek is seasonal creek that is fed by multiple springs and drains into Lake Tahoe at Hidden Beach. Multiple fuels reduction projects and understory burning have occurred adjacent to the creek over the last 20 years, with light thinning occurring in the riparian vegetation 15 years ago. Recent mortality in both white fir and red fir from bark beetles, combined with declining riparian vegetation due to conifer competition, has created hazardous conditions. This projects objectives will be achieved through a combination of hand thinning, pile building, and mastication.

ProjectName: Incline Village General Improvement District Fuels Reduction Project
LeadImplementerName: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
ProjectDescription: This project will focus on reducing hazardous fuels and maintaining healthy forest stands on land owned by the Incline Village General Improvement District.

ProjectName: Northstar Community Services District Wood Energy Facility
ProjectDescription: Northstar Community Services District is seeking to increase the scope and scale of its fuels management and defensible space programs through the development of a Wood Energy Facility project that will both reduce environmental impacts and minimize operating costs by creating a local use for otherwise non-merchantable biomass material. The project aims to serve as a valuable demonstration project for the greater Tahoe-Truckee region, acting as a catalyst for similar projects that could be replicated within the Tahoe-Truckee region as well as in other rural mountain and ski resort communities.

ProjectName: Kings Beach to Tahoe Vista - Pam Emmerich Memorial Pinedrop Trail
ProjectDescription: Reconstruct 1.5 miles of Class I bike and pedestrian trail from CA State Highway 267/Pinedrop Lane in Kings Beach, CA to the North Tahoe Regional Park in Tahoe Vista, CA

ProjectName: North Tahoe Regional Park to Tahoe Vista - Snow Creek Trail Connection
ProjectDescription: Construct a 0.5 mile Class I bike and pedestrian trail connection from the North Tahoe Regional Park/North Tahoe Trail Segment 1 junction south to National Avenue and the Tahoe Vista Recreation Area in Tahoe Vista, CA.

ProjectName: Bike and Pedestrian Facilities Operations and Maintenance - NTPUD
Watershed: Griff Creek, Tahoe Vista, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Carnelian Bay Creek, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Lake Forest Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Blackwood Creek, Eagle Rock, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, General Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: This is the NTPUD annual cost to operate and maintain the Class 1 Multi-Use Trail Systems in Kings Beach and Tahoe Vista, owned by Placer County. Operation and maintenance activities vary by jurisdiction and include, but are not limited to, sweeping, pavement maintenance, vegetation management,  trash removal, and snow removal. This O&M spans a 5-year period.

ProjectName: Tranquility Estates Fuels Treament and Stream Restoration
ProjectDescription:
Fuels reduction and stream restoration of up to 100 acres of fuel reduction work on a 200-acre private parcel to reduce wildfire risk, restore functions on McFaul Creek, and remove invasive weeds. 
Fuel treatments would include thinning of overstory trees, slash piling and burning. Understory brush would be cut, piled and burned, masticated, or chipped. 
Stream restoration would include performing low-impact process-based restoration water quality improvements while simultaneously performing fuels reduction within the SEZ.

ProjectName: Zephyr Heights Community Defensible Space
ProjectDescription: Fuels reduction treatment on a minimum of 75 acres of private parcels located within the Wildland Urban Interface (WUI) of Zephyr Cove, Nevada. This project collaborates with private landowners to implement defensible space and fuels reduction treatments on their properties. The project emphasizes community empowerment through education and outreach efforts that promote fire-adapted practices. This includes the formation of a Firewise site in partnership with Zephyr Cove residents.

ProjectName: Glenbrook Shaded Fuel Break Project
ProjectDescription:
This project was completed on August 28, 2025 to improve defensible space for Glenbrook, the US Highway 50 primary evacuation corridor, and East Shore Tahoe tourist assets by:
 
creating and sustaining a fuel break on GHOA General Forest and privately owned land parcels adjacent to US Highway 50.

creating and sustaining 200 ft fuel breaks on GHOA General Forest lands and privately owned land parcels located between Glenbrook and USFS parcels west of Spooner Summit, NV.

The project utilized 2025 Lake Tahoe-Community Wildfire Protection Plan mitigation strategies to reduce combustible fuels via mastication and hand crew work on approximately 60.89 acres of privately owned land.

ProjectName: Hogan Court Drainage Improvement Project
ProjectDescription: The project includes installation of a new storm drain junction box at an existing NDOT outlet located upslope of 699 Hogan Court and approximately 440 linear feet of underground storm drain pipe, connecting to the existing storm drain system at the intersection of Hogan Court and Titlist Drive. The project intends to reduce SR 431 embankment erosion and improve storm water conveyance. The storm drain alignment will traverse NDOT right-of-way, the private property at 699 Hogan Court, and Washoe County ROW. The project is in collaboration with NDOT, Washoe County, NTCD, and private property owners of 699 Hogan Court.

ProjectName: Glenbrook - Yerington Area Tree Thinning Project
ProjectDescription: This defensible space enhancement project with the Tahoe Douglas Fire Protection District thinned trees on 42 acres of land owned by 40 different individuals.  Goal was to restore parcel forests to a healthier density.  At the conclusion of project, defensible space around homes was expanded. Lean, clean, green zones are have been enhanced among closely spaced cottage and single family homes.  This project aligns with the Lake Tahoe - Community Wildfire Protection Plan and reduces wildfire risk in a designated Highest Priority Tier 1 Zone.

The existing access route will be maintained to ensure consistent site circulation. The expansion will be physically integrated with the existing skate park to provide a continuous riding surface and cohesive design, supporting efficient user flow and operational functionality.

Project has been combined with 02.01.01.0154 North Lake Tahoe Division CWPP Implementation Project.  Reporting can be found at https://www.laketahoeinfo.org/Project/DetailByName/North_Lake_Tahoe_Division_CWPP_Implementation_and_Completion_Project

The objective of this fuels reduction project is to create a continuous, landscape-scale treatment area that reduces wildfire risk, enhances suppression opportunities, and improves community safety within the Incline Village WUI.

ProjectName: Upper Truckee Marsh South Project
ProjectDescription: A multi-benefit project that has restoration, public access, and forestry elements. The Conservancy aims to restore wetlands by removing fill placed from historic development, including over eight feet of fill over four acres at a former motel and two acres at a former maintenance yard. Additionally, the Conservancy is considering stabilizing banks, removing encroached conifers, and enhancing meadows. The Conservancy is also evaluating opportunities to enhance a portion of the South Tahoe Bikeway and provide other public access amenities.

ProjectName: Lyons Ranch Fuel Hazard Reduction
ProjectDescription: The Lyons Ranch Fuel Hazard Reduction Project consists of manual and mechanical fuel hazard reduction treatments on 132 acres (33 acres of manual and 99 acres of mechanical) within the Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) in the south shore area of the Lake Tahoe Basin on Conservancy owned lands in El Dorado County. The treatments would reduce fuel loads near residential structures and are identified as priority treatment areas in the recently released Tahoe Basin CWPP. The project is designed to modify expected fire behavior/intensity in the treatment area and will serve to reduce wildfire risk to the adjacent residential south shore communities along Pioneer Trail.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Large Acreage Fuel Hazard Reduction
ProjectDescription: The Tahoe Keys Large Acreage (TKLA) Project consists of manual and mastication fuel reduction treatments on Conservancy and LTBMU owned land within the Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) in the south shore area of the Lake Tahoe Basin in the City of South Lake Tahoe. The treatments would reduce fuel loads near residential structures and are identified as priority treatment areas in the recently released Tahoe Basin CWPP. The project is designed to modify expected fire behavior/intensity in the treatment area and will serve to reduce wildfire risk to the adjacent residential south shore neighborhood of Tahoe

ProjectName: Upper Kingsbury Fire Adapted Community
ProjectDescription: This three-year project will help at least 200 privately owned properties (approximately 70 acres) in the Upper Kingsbury community achieve Defensible Space compliance through home inspections, vegetation treatment, chipping services, and compostable material drop-off. The project will reduce wildfire risk by addressing cost barriers that prevent property owners from completing defensible space work. Efforts include coordinated outreach, contractor support, partial reimbursements, and Firewise community engagement to promote long-term compliance and neighborhood-wide wildfire resilience.

ProjectName: Pope Marsh Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Project
ProjectDescription: The purpose of the project is to remove aquatic invasive plants (AIP) in Pope Marsh, and exclude plant fragments growing in Lake Tallac from flowing into and infesting the marsh and subsequently, Lake Tahoe. Pope Marsh is identified in the Lake Tahoe Region Aquatic Invasive Species Action Agenda 2021-2030 as a priority project. A survey conducted in July 2023 by Tahoe RCD’s contracted divers detected Eurasian watermilfoil (Myriophyllum spicatum) growing at various densities within a 1.8-acre area. In 2025, survey and hand removal of AIP was conducted by contracted divers and a metal screen was installed on top of the weir separating Pope Marsh from Lake Tallac to prevent further infestation.

ProjectName: Forest Health and White Bark Pine Mapping and Condition Assessment
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, U.S. Forest Service - Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Third Creek, Incline Creek, Wood Creek, Griff Creek, Second Creek, Tahoe Vista, First Creek, Burnt Cedar Creek, Mill Creek, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Tunnel Creek, Carnelian Bay Creek, Bonpland, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Sand Harbor, Lake Forest Creek, Marlette Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Secret Harbor Creek, Bliss Creek, Deadman Point, Slaughter House, Blackwood Creek, Glenbrook Creek, Eagle Rock, North Logan House Creek, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, Logan House Creek, General Creek, Cave Rock, Lincoln Creek, Meeks Creek, North Zephyr Creek, Skyland, Zephyr Creek, Sierra Creek, Mcfaul Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, South Zephyr Creek, Burke Creek, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: The purpose of this project is to improve the understanding of extent and health of occupied whitebark pine stands within the Lake Tahoe Basin to support habitat conservation and recovery plans. Existing habitat maps are sufficient for identifying coarse localities where whitebark pine dominated stands occur, but extent of dominant, co-dominant, and mixed stands is lacking. Ground based mapping is limited in whitebark pine stands due to steep and rugged terrain that is difficult or infeasible to traverse on foot. Recent research has demonstrated use of unmanned aerial vehicles to map whitebark pine presence and mortality. The objective of this project is to produce spatial products.

ProjectName: South Shore Offshore Aquatic Invasive Plant Planning and Control
ProjectDescription: Enhanced aquatic invasive plant monitoring has revealed sparse areas of plant infestations between previously defined project areas. The South Shore Offshore Aquatic Invasive Plant Planning and Control project implements a new strategy to evaluate, plan, and implement control treatments in aquatic invasive plant-infested areas over a larger landscape vs. individual, specific areas. Work commenced in 2025 in the following unit locations: Taylor-Tallac offshore, Camp Richardson, Edgewood 1, Edgewood 2, and Nevada Beach.

ProjectName: Elk Point and Round Hill Rock Cribs Aquatic Invasive Plant Control
ProjectDescription: From May to July 2025, divers conducting surveillance work north of Nevada Beach detected thousands of aquatic invasive plant fragments floating on the water surface and in the water column. Thousands of these fragments settled and rooted offshore in numbers and distribution far exceeding previous observations in this location. This discovery spurred a rapid response, and divers spent several days pulling the rooted plants and removing fragments. This project proposes to conduct site assessments and plant removal dive visits at this location and sites north of Elk Point in 2026, to ensure that no aquatic invasive plants are infesting the area.

ProjectName: Tahoe Keys Interim Treatment and Monitoring
ProjectDescription: Implementation of treatment and monitoring in the Tahoe Keys Lagoons following the completion of the Tahoe Keys Control Methods Test in 2024 while development and scoping is underway for a full Tahoe Keys treatment in the coming years.

ProjectName: Managing Increased Recreation on Tahoe's Trails - Tahoe Rim Trail Association
Jurisdiction: City of South Lake Tahoe, Douglas County, NV, El Dorado County, CA, Placer County, CA, Washoe County, NV, Carson City County, NV, Alpine County
Watershed: Griff Creek, Tahoe Vista, East Stateline Point, Carnelian Canyon, Kings Beach, Ward Creek, Watson, Carnelian Bay Creek, Cedar Flats, Barton Creek, Dollar Creek, Burton Creek, Lake Forest Creek, Tahoe State Park, Truckee River, Blackwood Creek, Eagle Rock, Madden Creek, Homewood Creek, Quail Lake Creek, Mckinney Creek, General Creek, Meeks Creek, Sierra Creek, Lonely Gulch Creek, Paradise Flat, Rubicon Creek, Bliss State Park, Edgewood Creek, Bijou Park, Eagle Creek, Cascade Creek, Bijou Creek, Tallac Creek, Upper Truckee River, Trout Creek, Camp Richardson, Taylor Creek, Lake Tahoe Waterbody
ProjectDescription: Trail counter data collected by the Tahoe Rim Trail Association (TRTA) reports that recreation on the Tahoe Rim Trail increased from an estimated 400,000 annual users in 2016 to 700,000 in 2022. Despite this viral growth in recreation, resources to maintain sustainable trails in the Tahoe Basin remain limited. The TRTA will improve the Tahoe Rim Trail System along the existing trail corridor by installing structures such as rock walls and drainages that ensure the environmental sustainability of Tahoe’s booming recreation economy, keeping trails open to all while preserving the natural environment that people come to the Basin to enjoy.

ProjectName: New Purchase of a High Efficiency Sweeper - El Dorado County

ProjectDescription: High-efficiency street sweepers are included in the Environmental Improvement Program under the improving air quality priority, although it is recognized that they have multiple threshold benefits.

ProjectDescription: Reduce wildland fire fuels across 46 parcels owned by Placer County (53 acres total). The parcels are spread across the WUI area from the CA/NV state line to the Placer County/ El Dorado County line.  This project will contribute to community safety and wildfire resilience by hand thinning vegetation, removing ladder fuels, removing hazardous trees, and reducing the buildup of down woody material. The project is funded by the California Tahoe Conservancy.

ProjectName: SR 28 Spooner Mobility Hub and AIS Inspection Station - Vertical Elements (phase 2)
ProjectDescription: The project builds on the Nevada Department of Transportation (03.02.01.0064) civil work includes the design and construction of the vertical elements for the transit mobility hub, restrooms, and an AIS inspection station.

ProjectName: North 1st & 2nd Creek Fuels Reduction Project
LeadImplementerName: North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District
ProjectDescription: The objective of this hazardous fuels reduction project is to strategically tie in with three recently completed fuels reduction projects, creating a contiguous, landscape-scale treatment area within the wildland-urban interface (WUI) of Incline Village. A total of $224,252 in grant funds will be sub-awarded to the North Lake Tahoe Fire Protection District (NLTFPD) to implement hazardous fuels reduction treatments across 83.3 acres in the North First Creek area of Incline Village. These funds will be matched on a 1:1 basis by the Incline Village General Improvement District (IVGID), ensuring a fully funded and cost-effective approach to project completion.

ProjectName: Cole Property Hazardous Fuels Reduction and Forest Health Project
ProjectDescription: The Cole Unit Hazardous Fuels Reduction Project is located within the city limits of South Lake Tahoe and adjacent to U.S. Forest Service land. The project is designed to reduce hazardous fuels, improve forest structure, and increase wildfire resilience within the wildland–urban interface. Treatments will include thin-from-below operations and cut-to-length harvesting to reduce fuel continuity, improve stand vigor, and enhance defensibility near developed areas.

ProjectName: SR 89/Tahoma Pedestrian Crossing Improvements (SHOPP Minor B)
ProjectDescription: Near Tahoma, at the intersection of Pine Street. Install Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB). EA: 03-2N810

ProjectName: Van Sickle Bi-State Park Campground
LeadImplementerName: Nevada Tahoe Resource Team – Nevada Division of State Parks
ProjectDescription: Van Sickle Bi-State Park is currently undergoing major infrastructure and recreation renovations, including the construction of a park maintenance facility, staff housing, and the future establishment of a park visitor center. NDSP plans for the establishment of this campground to be the final phase of renovations to take place.
